state_of_play.narrative:
THE UNITED STATES AND IRAN EXCHANGED FIRE AGAIN AND THE MARKET PRICED IT AS AN INFLATION EVENT, NOT A WAR ONE. US forces struck two rocket launchers on Iran's Larak Island on Sunday 30 August, the first publicly acknowledged strike on Iranian positions since late July, and Iranian state media reported retaliation against US bases in Jordan. The S&P 500 settled 7,686.14 on Monday, down 0.33% on Friday's 7,711.76, the Dow lost 374.09 points to 53,185.90 and the Nasdaq slipped 0.12% to 26,370.89 - and all three still closed August higher. Brent settled $90.49 and US crude gained more than 3%. The important reaction was not in equities at all: the ten-year Treasury yield settled 4.758%, its highest in nineteen months, and European gas passed EUR 70 a megawatt-hour for the first time since January 2023. An oil shock that arrives while a central bank is already arguing about raising rates is read as a reason to raise them.

THE RATE ARGUMENT HAS MOVED FROM A COIN FLIP TO A FAVOURITE IN THREE SESSIONS. CME FedWatch put the odds of a September increase at 66.1% on Monday, against a near-70% chance of no change before Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote on Friday. Not every measure agrees - one fed funds futures read sits near 56% and traders on Kalshi are at 48% - and that dispersion is itself informative, because a market that has doubled its odds on a speech rather than a print is holding a view it has not yet tested. The test is Friday 4 September's US employment report, expected near 55,000. The repricing remains concentrated at the short end: the thirty-year, already close to a nineteen-year high, has barely moved, and the dollar index settled 99.43. Barclays, Societe Generale and Deutsche Bank all forecast increases in September and December, an ECB policymaker has pointed to a September rise to 2.5%, and the Bank of England enters its own September meeting divided while British shop prices rise at their fastest in more than two years.

THE MEMORY MARKET PRODUCED ITS TWO LARGEST FACTS OF THE MONTH ON THE SAME DAY, POINTING OPPOSITE WAYS. Samsung has committed roughly 70% of its memory production capacity to long-term agreements running to 2031, with Microsoft, Nvidia and Google named among the counterparties; the contracted price of a 36GB HBM3E module runs 500,000 to 700,000 Korean won against about 2.87m won on the spot market. Buyers accepting five-year commitments at a fifth of spot are pricing a shortage that lasts. Against that, China's ChangXin Memory Technologies has begun small-batch production of HBM3E, with Alibaba's T-Head and Cambricon testing it and commercial integration targeted for 2027. That is the substitution argument arriving on the ground this case actually stands on, after last week's LPDDR6 report which was mobile memory. It is one generation behind the HBM4 now in mass production at Samsung, SK hynix and Micron, and reporting puts CXMT three to five years behind technically with low yields. Both facts are trade press rather than filings and both are carried as reported.

NVIDIA IS FINANCING ITS OWN SUPPLY CHAIN, AND THE INSTRUMENT IS ALWAYS A CONVERTIBLE. Nvidia is taking $3.5bn of MediaTek's $3.9bn overseas convertible bond - about 90% of the largest such offering in Taiwan's capital market history, and its largest direct investment outside the United States. The stated purpose is custom silicon that plugs into Nvidia-based data centres. It is the same shape as the $2.0bn of convertible preferred stock Nvidia took in Marvell on 31 March, a transaction that recirculated as fresh news last week and was in fact five months old. Elsewhere in the stack, SK hynix is reported to be evaluating Intel's foundry for HBM4E base dies, a Chinese court froze $300m of Nexperia's assets in the Wingtech case, and Bank of America now sizes TSMC's 2027 capital spending at up to $85bn. TSMC's own dated commitment this week was about light rather than price: a vice-president told SEMICON Taiwan that silicon photonics penetration passes 50% in 2027 and co-packaged optics mass production begins in the second half.

THE POWER CONSTRAINT HAS MOVED INSIDE THE FOUNDRY. Elon Musk confirmed on 29 August that SpaceX is building a foundry in Bastrop, Texas to cast hot-section turbine blades and vanes - the nickel-superalloy parts that run at 1,650 to 1,980 degrees, which only a handful of plants worldwide can make, and whose scarcity has pushed large-turbine delivery into 2030. The stated gain is up to eighteen months, and the same alloys and furnaces serve rocket-engine turbopumps. In the same week SLB agreed to buy Kelvion for $3.4bn, moving an oilfield services group into data-centre heat exchange, and Holtec began loading fuel at Palisades, the first shut American reactor to reach that step on the way back. Three separate buyers of the constrained physical part rather than of the headline generation. Siemens Energy, meanwhile, confirmed that Omterra is its new group name uniting the core business and Siemens Gamesa from later this year, removing about EUR 300m of annual licence fees, against a record EUR 162bn order backlog and a EUR 10bn divestment drawing private equity bidders.

THE ENERGY PREMIUM HAS FINISHED ITS MOVE OUT OF CRUDE AND INTO GAS. The Dutch TTF front-month contract reached an intraday high of EUR 70.49 a megawatt-hour on 31 August, a three-and-a-half-year high, with European storage 63% full in the final week of August - well below the seasonal average, in the middle of the refill season. Goldman Sachs has said that a sustained Gulf disruption forcing European buyers to outbid Asia could carry prices toward EUR 100. Crude went the other way within a day: Brent settled $90.49 on Monday and traded near $88.5 on Tuesday morning as Washington signalled possible sanctions easing. The asymmetry is physical. A cargo of crude can be re-routed and a liquefaction train cannot, so a Gulf disruption prices into gas and stays there, and Europe pays for it directly through industrial costs and the household bill. US strategic reserves are reported at their lowest since 1982.

THE DEFENCE CONSTRAINT FINALLY GOT A STRUCTURAL ANSWER, WITH ONE CONDITION ATTACHED. The Department of War announced seven-year framework agreements with General Dynamics Ordnance and Tactical Systems and Lockheed Martin on 31 August, initiating multiyear procurement contracts intended to triple PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement output and quadruple THAAD interceptor output; Lockheed separately holds a seven-year undefinitized contract action worth up to $35bn on THAAD from 24 June. All month the binding constraint in this cluster has been delivery rather than orders, and a seven-year framework is long enough for a supplier to buy tooling against. The release states the condition itself: funding remains subject to annual appropriations, and the appropriations deadline is 30 September. Ukraine's defence minister is seeking an early EU loan against a $27bn gap and Poland is shifting toward domestic production.

EUROPE'S SATELLITE PROGRAMME PLACED ITS FIRST BIG CONTRACT AND, UNLIKE ITS ROCKETS, IT WENT TO A LISTED COMPANY. SES awarded OHB nearly EUR 1bn on 31 August for eighteen medium-earth-orbit platforms for IRIS2, the first major award under the concession, whose implementation phase began on 6 August. First launches are expected in 2029 and service from 2030, within a 348-satellite constellation whose low-orbit segment Eutelsat leads. Four days earlier the European Space Agency's EUR 543.6m of launcher contracts went entirely to private companies, so European sovereign space money now has a listed route on the satellite side and none at all on the launch side. Both facts belong together, and the revenue in each case belongs to the next decade.

A COURT AND A FUNDING ROUND GAVE PREDICTION MARKETS TWO OPPOSITE ANSWERS IN THREE DAYS. On 28 August the Ninth Circuit denied Kalshi, Crypto.com and Robinhood injunctions against the Nevada Gaming Control Board, holding sports event contracts are likely bets rather than federally regulated swaps and that commodities law probably does not preempt state gaming rules - contradicting a Third Circuit ruling and sending the question toward the Supreme Court, where traders now price a 52% chance of review. British Columbia's regulator has reached the same conclusion as Nevada. Three days later 1789 Capital led a $1bn round valuing Polymarket at $21bn, up from $15bn in April, after Intercontinental Exchange completed a $1.6bn investment; Kalshi was valued at $22bn in May. A sector that has roughly quadrupled in private value inside a year has had its central premise moved into litigation, and the purest exposure on both sides is private.

THE ACCESS RAIL INTO PRIVATE CREDIT AND ITS LIQUIDITY ARE STILL MOVING APART. Bloomberg reported an Australian property collapse as the first real test for retail private credit in that market. It arrives alongside Apollo's redemption cap - imposed in June after exit requests reached 16.8% - and MA Financial's 1% monthly cap from 25 August, in the same month the Financial Conduct Authority authorised the Legal and General and WTW private credit long-term asset fund for defined-contribution pension schemes and Goldman Sachs began preparing a retail private equity fund. The order in which a saver meets these two facts is the wrong way round: the wrapper opens first and the gate is discovered later. Elsewhere in capital flows, US spot bitcoin funds took about $3.2bn in their best week since October while the Senate procedural vote on the CLARITY Act, due 15 September, is priced at roughly a 14% chance of passing, and the Bank of England signalled easier sterling stablecoin rules while the US Treasury proposed forcing American exchanges to audit foreign stablecoin issuers or delist them.

ONE ITEM THAT READ AS THIS WEEK'S NEWS WAS FIVE WEEKS OLD. The FDA's market authorisation for Johnson & Johnson's OTTAVA robotic surgical system, the first table-integrated soft-tissue robot, surfaced in trade coverage on 31 August; the De Novo authorisation was granted in July. It is a genuine challenge to a market one company has held largely alone, and it is not new. Two other dated firsts do stand: Tennessee issued the first US state licence for a commercial fusion plant, to Type One Energy for a prototype commissioning in 2029 and a 400 megawatt stellarator at the Tennessee Valley Authority's Bull Run complex that could start construction in 2028; and Portugal opened a consultation targeting 6.9 gigawatts of grid storage by 2030, days after SK On's 9 gigawatt-hour American contract worth about $1.09bn.

sections.line: Monday's session was the first to settle since Friday and it was mildly negative: the S&P 500 closed 7,686.14, down 0.33%, the Dow lost 374.09 points to 53,185.90 and the Nasdaq eased 0.12% to 26,370.89, with all three still finishing August higher. Volatility rose but stayed low, the VIX settling 14.92 against 14.43 on Friday. London was shut for the bank holiday, so the FTSE 100's most recent close remains Friday's 10,824.26 and it reopens today; the STOXX 600 settled 651.10.

Futures moved from a coin flip to a favourite in three sessions. CME FedWatch put a September increase at 66.1% on Monday against a near-70% chance of no change before the Jackson Hole keynote, though other measures read nearer 56% and prediction-market traders 48%. The ten-year settled 4.758%, its highest in nineteen months, while the thirty-year barely moved and the dollar index closed 99.43. The decision is on 16 September and Friday's employment report, expected near 55,000, is the first hard evidence either way.

The Dutch TTF gas contract reached EUR 70.49 a megawatt-hour intraday, a three-and-a-half-year high, with European storage 63% full during the refill season and Goldman Sachs pointing to EUR 100 if a Gulf disruption forces Europe to outbid Asia. Crude moved the other way within a day: Brent settled $90.49 on Monday and traded near $88.5 on Tuesday morning on talk of sanctions easing. Gold settled $4,431.10 on Monday, 1.05% lower, and was near $4,493 the next morning, still closing its best month since January.

Samsung has committed roughly 70% of its memory capacity to agreements running to 2031 at about a fifth of spot prices, while China's CXMT began small-batch production of HBM3E with Alibaba's T-Head and Cambricon testing it - one generation behind the HBM4 now in mass production elsewhere. Nvidia took $3.5bn of MediaTek's convertible bond, and TSMC put a date on co-packaged optics: silicon photonics past half of advanced packaging in 2027. SpaceX is building a turbine-blade foundry in Texas to attack the casting shortage that has pushed large-turbine delivery into 2030.

US forces struck two rocket launchers on Iran's Larak Island on 30 August, the first publicly acknowledged strike since late July, and Iranian state media reported attacks on US bases in Jordan. The Department of War signed seven-year agreements to triple Patriot PAC-3 MSE and quadruple THAAD interceptor production, with funding still subject to annual appropriations. Ukraine is lobbying Washington on a Russia sanctions bill and seeking an early EU loan against a $27bn gap.

Washington extended export controls to tungsten and to battery black mass, reaching the recycling feedstock Chinese processors depend on, while four separate Western rare-earth consolidations closed in a week. Canada's counter-tariffs take effect on 8 September and Ottawa has tied any settlement to protecting its car industry. The rule that would make remote access to controlled AI chips a licensable event is still expected to reach industry by the end of September.

Palo Alto Networks reports today and is the test of whether one security vendor's record quarter was a sector turn. Tesla's Cybercab production event is on 3 September, the US August employment report on 4 September, and Hanwha's exclusive look at Austal USA expires around 8 September. The Senate procedural vote on the CLARITY Act is 15 September, the Federal Reserve decides on 16 September, and Micron's fiscal fourth quarter and the US appropriations deadline both fall on 30 September.

crash_risk.read: Held at 65, and every bucket that moved this week moved on the price of money. Futures now put a September Federal Reserve increase at 66%, roughly double where they sat before Friday's Jackson Hole keynote, and the ten-year Treasury settled 4.758% on Monday, its highest in nineteen months. An exchange of fire between US and Iranian forces on 30 August added an inflation impulse rather than a risk-off one: European gas reached EUR 70.49 a megawatt-hour, a three-and-a-half-year high, and Brent settled $90.49 before easing back toward $88.5 the next morning. Against all of that the market's own stress gauges barely reacted. Volatility settled 14.92, up about 3.4% on Friday and still close to a one-month low, credit spreads are calm at roughly 260 basis points on high yield and 79 on investment grade, and funding conditions remain loose. The equity move was small: the S&P 500 lost a third of a percent and August still closed higher. Breadth stays the weak reading, with concentration elevated and about 62% of members above their two-hundred-day average. Valuation remains the heaviest bucket, because a Shiller multiple of 41.8 and a Buffett indicator near 217% both assume a discount rate that falls, and the discount rate is now arguing the other way in public. The risk that would actually break something is still off-index and off-balance-sheet: the largest spenders on artificial intelligence are expected to burn cash into 2027 and to fund the gap in the bond market, and European Central Bank analysts have now warned that the scale of that issuance is raising euro-area borrowing costs and that credit ratings may be understating the risk. What would change this reading is a weak employment print on Friday that takes the rate argument away, or a widening in credit spreads that says the funding channel has finally noticed.

buckets.summary: Still the heaviest bucket, and the pressure on it is arithmetic. A Shiller multiple of 41.8 and a Buffett indicator near 217% are both at stress, with forward earnings near 20.6 times and a thin excess yield of 1.4%. Each of those numbers assumes a discount rate that falls. Futures now price a two-thirds chance that the discount rate rises this month instead, and the ten-year is at a nineteen-month high, so the denominator is moving against the multiple rather than for it.

sectors.rationale: Nvidia is financing the suppliers who build to its standard. It is taking $3.5bn of MediaTek's $3.9bn overseas convertible bond, about 90% of the largest such offering in Taiwan's capital market history and its largest direct investment outside the United States, for custom silicon that plugs into Nvidia-based data centres; MediaTek rose about 10% on 1 September. The instrument is the same convertible structure as the $2.0bn taken in Marvell on 31 March. TSMC put dates on packaging rather than price - silicon photonics past 50% penetration in 2027, co-packaged optics in mass production in the second half - while the reported 2027 wafer price increases remain supply-chain reporting rather than a company statement.

Gold settled $4,431.10 on Monday 31 August, down 1.05%, and traded near $4,493 the next morning. That is a second consecutive settled session in which the rate path has beaten the official bid: futures moved to a 66% chance of a September Federal Reserve increase and the ten-year reached a nineteen-month high. The month still finished as the best since January, up about 11%, and the structural floor is unchanged - record second-quarter official buying of 289 tonnes worth about $47.4bn and twenty consecutive months of Chinese accumulation totalling 2,346 tonnes. The level sits 20.8% below the peak of 29 January 2026.

The constraint has moved inside the machine. Elon Musk confirmed on 29 August that SpaceX is building a foundry in Bastrop, Texas to cast hot-section turbine blades and vanes, the nickel-superalloy parts only a handful of plants worldwide can make and whose scarcity has pushed large-turbine delivery into 2030; the stated gain is up to eighteen months. In the same week SLB agreed to buy Kelvion for $3.4bn and Baker Hughes took an order for 76 turbines. Four authorities have now decided that a large load pays for its own power, Delaware by legislation on 28 August, and Siemens Energy confirmed it will trade as Omterra from later this year against a record EUR 162bn backlog.

Two facts of opposite sign landed on the same day. Samsung has committed roughly 70% of its memory capacity to agreements running to 2031, with Microsoft, Nvidia and Google named among the counterparties, at 500,000 to 700,000 Korean won a 36GB HBM3E module against about 2.87m won spot - buyers pricing a shortage that lasts. Against that, China's CXMT began small-batch production of HBM3E, with Alibaba's T-Head and Cambricon testing it and commercial integration targeted for 2027; that is one generation behind the HBM4 in mass production at Samsung, SK hynix and Micron, and CXMT is reported three to five years behind technically with low yields. Contracted demand is unchanged - Nvidia's supply commitments rose from $119bn to $279bn in a quarter - and Micron's fiscal fourth quarter on 30 September is the next hard print.

The foundry has dated the transition this sector is waiting for. A TSMC vice-president told SEMICON Taiwan on 31 August that silicon photonics penetration passes 50% in 2027 and that co-packaged optics mass production begins in the second half, alongside an upgraded 3DFabric platform with CoWoS-integrated transistor volume projected to grow about 48 times by 2029. That is a dated commitment from the company that has to build the packaging rather than a market projection. It also sharpens the risk: the listed transceiver names capture this demand while the optics stay on the board, and co-packaging is the move that puts them inside the package.

The delivery constraint has a seven-year answer. The Department of War announced framework agreements with General Dynamics Ordnance and Tactical Systems and Lockheed Martin on 31 August, initiating multiyear procurement contracts intended to triple PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement output and quadruple THAAD interceptor output; Lockheed separately holds a seven-year undefinitized contract action worth up to $35bn on THAAD from 24 June. The release states its own condition: funding is subject to annual appropriations, with the deadline on 30 September. In Europe, Romania has drawn its first EUR 2.5bn under SAFE, Italy has requested EUR 8bn, and Ukraine is seeking an early EU loan against a $27bn gap.

The instrument has widened from the mine to the scrap heap. New US controls on tungsten and on battery black mass are reported to be squeezing Chinese recyclers who depend on imported feedstock, reaching a step in the chain China had cornered without anyone legislating about it. Four Western consolidations closed in the same week - Energy Fuels' $299m purchase of an Australian producer, Mkango's acquisition of Remloy, Neo Performance's partnership with Carester, and Astron's US export licence - alongside $75m for magnet recycling. The equities did not follow: Energy Fuels fell 6.5% and Aclara 5.6% during the week, which is the gap between policy and price this sector has carried since it was created.

Europe's secure-satellite programme placed its first major contract and it went to a listed builder: SES awarded OHB nearly EUR 1bn on 31 August for eighteen medium-earth-orbit platforms for IRIS2, whose implementation phase began on 6 August, with first launches expected in 2029 and service from 2030. Four days earlier the European Space Agency's EUR 543.6m of launcher contracts went entirely to private companies. Sovereign European space money now has a listed route on the satellite side and none on the launch side. Rocket Lab sold Kepler a full Neutron flight before the rocket has flown and won a $12m Space Force contract; the company's own words still put pad delivery in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The threat record keeps setting records and the spending evidence still comes from one issuer. CISA flagged actively exploited PaperCut flaws and added Linux kernel and JFrog Artifactory vulnerabilities to its exploited catalogue after an AI agent exploitation - the first time the mechanism has been an agent rather than a person in this record. Broadcom launched security products for enterprise AI agents. The case still rests on CrowdStrike's quarter: revenue of $1.47bn up 26%, annual recurring revenue of $5.84bn up 25% and record net new recurring revenue of $332.8m. Palo Alto Networks reports on 1 September and is the named sector test.

Flows and rules moved in opposite directions, and the split is now geographic. US spot bitcoin funds took about $3.2bn in their best week since October before a $202m outflow day, with bitcoin near $79,000 against a rising real yield. The Senate procedural vote on the CLARITY Act is set for 15 September and traders price it at roughly a 14% chance; the Treasury has proposed forcing US exchanges to audit foreign stablecoin issuers or delist them; the BIS says stablecoins are not ready for everyday payments and the IMF warns on emerging-market monetary sovereignty. Against that, the Bank of England signalled easier sterling stablecoin rules and Singapore proposed a regime covering foreign issuers.

The premium has finished its move out of crude and into gas. The Dutch TTF front-month contract reached an intraday EUR 70.49 a megawatt-hour on 31 August, its highest since January 2023, with European storage 63% full during the refill season and Goldman Sachs pointing to EUR 100 if a Gulf disruption forces Europe to outbid Asia. Crude round-tripped inside a day: Brent settled $90.49 on Monday after US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers, then traded near $88.5 on Tuesday on talk of sanctions easing. Very large crude carriers on the Gulf-to-China route remain at a record $647,000 a day and US strategic reserves are reported at their lowest since 1982.

A restart reached fuel, which is the step that makes it real: Holtec began loading fuel at Palisades in Michigan on 31 August, the furthest any shut American reactor has come back toward generation. The Army's Janus programme continues to disburse, with up to $2.2bn committed through fiscal 2031 across five vendors and five bases for more than twenty microreactors; Radiant's share is reported at $750m by a single outlet, and the vendor figure and the programme figure have not been reconciled. SLB agreed to buy Kelvion for $3.4bn, moving an oilfield services group into data-centre heat exchange. US uranium output has tripled and still does not cover domestic demand.

The financing question has acquired a European supervisor. ECB analysts warned that the scale of US technology issuance in the euro bond market could raise European borrowing costs, and a separate warning covered EU pension funds buying into the American AI build against credit ratings that may understate future risk. Until now the crowding-out argument had been made about Treasuries by fund managers. The operating numbers stayed mixed: IREN reported a $684m loss alongside a frontier AI contract and Nebius was downgraded after its run, while CoreWeave's 112% revenue growth to $2.58bn and Oracle's $638bn backlog are unchanged. S&P Global Ratings still expects all six of the largest AI spenders to burn cash through 2027.

The approvals are in autonomy and the humanoid evidence is still second-hand. Nevada has authorised up to 7,000 paid driverless vehicles across Tesla, Waymo and Uber, Waymo has begun street mapping in Munich for a late-2027 launch, and DiDi has started fully driverless trials with its next-generation robotaxi; Tesla's Cybercab production event falls on 3 September. A Waymo executive publicly argued that camera-only self-driving cannot see enough, which is the technical dispute the revenue case turns on. In humanoids, Digitimes counted shipments above 22,000 in the first half and Europe's first mass-production base began output in a China-Serbia joint venture - an aggregator count rather than a maker disclosing deployments.

drivers.trajLbl: Financing strain hardening while the demand question stays answered
drivers.oneLiner: Financing is the contested leg and a European supervisor has now named it: ECB analysts say US technology issuance is raising euro-area borrowing costs.
summary: The market's changing willingness to fund AI capital expenditure - and who gets paid for it.
Conversion is now printing as revenue at the recipients while the payers' commitments stay off balance sheet.

THE CONVERSION LEG IS NOW A REVENUE LINE RATHER THAN A PREPAYMENT PROMISE. CoreWeave's second quarter, dated 12 August, put revenue at $2.6bn, up 112% from $1.2bn, with a $104bn backlog against a $58.8bn market value; Nebius grew revenue 514% to $575m with the value of contracts won quadrupling. Both rose hard on the day, 19% and 34%.

AND THE TWO FINANCE IT DIFFERENTLY, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. Nebius funds 50-60% of the capital spending tied to major contracts from customer prepayments, above $9bn expected in 2026, and raised $4.5bn of convertibles on 19 August. CoreWeave carries more than $35bn of debt and rising interest expense against the same demand. Recipients are converting; how they pay for the next round is not settled.

THE FINANCING LEG IS UNCHANGED AND STILL CONTESTED. About $3tn of off-balance-sheet commitments across nine large technology companies - roughly five times their reported trailing capital spending - is unanswered, and NVIDIA's print on 26 August is the next thing that tests it.

THE SEPTEMBER PATH, PINNED TO INSTRUMENTS RATHER THAN TO COMMENTARY. The 16 September FOMC carries roughly 69% for no change and 31% for a 25bp increase on Polymarket, with CME FedWatch at 67.6% and 68.4% for a hold on 13 and 20 August. Funds stay at 3.50-3.75%.

AND THE LARGEST SCHEDULED INPUT BEFORE IT IS JACKSON HOLE. The Kansas City Fed's symposium runs 27-29 August at Jackson Lake Lodge on the theme of financial innovation and its implications for payments and policy, with about 120 central bankers from more than 70 countries attending. Kevin Warsh, sworn in on 22 May, gives the keynote at 10am ET on Friday 28 August - his first as chair. He has signalled he wants it to frame long-run questions rather than near-term policy, and 69% of surveyed fund managers expect a neutral tone.

The committee is hawkish in composition rather than in expected action: the Fed held 9-3 in July with three regional presidents dissenting in favour of an increase, and the Bank of England held at 3.75% on 30 July, 6-3, with Megan Greene, Catherine Mann and Huw Pill dissenting for a rise - its most hawkish split since 2016.

Watch the long end. The 10-year rose another 4bp to 4.74% through two sessions of equity strength, so it has stopped trading off risk appetite, and the Treasury's enlarged long-dated buybacks do not begin buying until 9 September.

summary: Electricity demand from AI, electrification and reshoring - the physical constraint the compute build runs into.

THE QUANTIFICATION HELD UP TO CHECKING, WHICH IS NOT ALWAYS THE OUTCOME. Morgan Stanley's estimate is corroborated across four independent outlets with a consistent decomposition: ~68 GW of US data-centre need across 2026-28, ~15 GW under construction and ~15 GW available or contracted, leaving a ~38 GW gap. It remains an ESTIMATE and the note itself has not been obtained; a November 2025 MS figure of 44 GW is also in circulation and is recorded. Additive and dated: grid connection now takes five to seven years in parts of the US, and MS's preferred fixes are gas turbines, fuel cells, colocation with operating nuclear plants and conversion of former bitcoin-mining sites.

THE ORDER BOOK COMPOUNDED AGAIN. GE Vernova's gas equipment backlog and slot reservations reached 116 GW at the end of the second quarter, from 100 GW three months earlier, on $16.7bn of Power orders in the quarter, up 134% organically, inside a $176bn total backlog - with at least 125 GW targeted under contract by year-end. Turbine slots are tight through 2030 across the three makers who between them control the market.

AND THE CONTESTED HALF-YEAR FIGURE NOW RECONCILES ARITHMETICALLY. Data-centre electrification orders of $2.4bn in the first quarter plus $2.7bn in the second is the ~$5bn attributed on 22 August to GE Vernova rather than to Eaton. The attribution stands on its own arithmetic as well as on the sources that settled it.

TWO OF THE THREE RHEINMETALL CONTRACTS ARE NOW CORROBORATED AND DATED 19 AUGUST. A Bundeswehr mobile-rescue-station order worth more than EUR 500m, and a Danish MASS decoy award of DKK 745m - about $116m - for Absalon and Iver Huitfeldt class frigates. The EUR 3.4bn Italian heavy-tank programme through the Leonardo Rheinmetall joint venture still rests on one aggregator.

THE MARITIME LEG HAS A COUNTERPARTY. The shipbuilding case rests on a 14 August national-security memorandum permitting foreign construction of US Navy vessels, and Congress has been legislating against that authority in both chambers since June: the House FY27 NDAA bars foreign construction of warships and combat-logistics vessels, and the Senate mark strips the presidential waiver while allowing up to two auxiliaries from foreign yards.

IT RESOLVED AGAINST A DEAL AND THE OTHER SIDE HAS NOW ANSWERED. Talks collapsed minutes before the midnight expiry and 50% Section 338 duties took effect at 00:01 ET on 22 August on about $20bn of Canadian goods - hockey sticks, building materials, liquors, certain clothing. Hours later Prime Minister Mark Carney set counter-tariffs on $20bn of American products from 8 September, aimed at steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper and electronics. Talks are suspended and none are scheduled.

THE SCOPE FIGURE SETTLES AT $20bn. Bloomberg, NPR, ABC and US News all carry $20bn, described as roughly 5% of Canadian exports to the United States, which resolves the wider $28bn number that circulated on Friday in favour of the majority.

AND THE OTHER SURVIVING INSTRUMENT WIDENED. A proclamation signed 13 August imposes 100% Section 232 duties on large, heavy or thermal-imaging-capable unmanned aircraft and 25% on most consumer drones. The frame is narrow instruments being used harder, not the broad wall returning: 232 and 338 are alive and expanding, and the emergency authority struck down on 20 February is gone.

THE NEW CANADIAN AUTO TARIFF IS A SEPARATE, LATER INSTRUMENT. Trump's 24 August announcement raises Canadian auto, truck and steel tariffs from a 25% baseline to 50%, effective 1 January 2027 - a distinct, forward-dated escalation layered alongside the Section 338 50% duties that have been in force on other goods since 22 August, not an immediate stack on top of them. Canada's own 8 September counter-tariffs on $20bn of US goods are re-confirmed across six-plus independent outlets.

THE G7 CAP IS REAL, IS DATED, AND IS A STRUCTURAL DRIVER RATHER THAN A HEADLINE. recorded and withheld on 21 August for want of a date: G7 leaders agreed at the Evian summit on 17 JUNE 2026 that no single country should supply more than 60% of their rare-earth and permanent-magnet imports by 2030, aiming to cut exposure to 50% as soon as possible thereafter. It is a 2030 target rather than an operative measure, and it is two months old - so it is carried as structure, not as this month's catalyst. Against China refining ~91% of the world's rare earths today, the gap between the target and the base is the whole opportunity.

THE SECOND FRONT IS OPTICS AND IT MOVED PRICES THIS MONTH. A Reuters report that the administration was preparing restrictions on Chinese-made optical transceivers used in data centres sent Applied Optoelectronics +17%, Coherent +11% and Lumentum +6% on 4 August. summary: Conflict, sanctions and the security of physical supply - and the price they put on energy.

THE ESCALATION LEG LANDED SOFTER THAN THREATENED, AND A DE-ESCALATION LEG HARDENED IN RESPONSE. Treasury Secretary Bessent's 24 August package sanctioned roughly sixty Iran-linked entities and vessels but deliberately excluded immediate secondary sanctions on Iran's trading partners, describing a 'cure period' and 'quiet diplomacy' rather than the toughest measures threatened three days earlier.

AND SO DOES THE DE-ESCALATION LEG, WHICH IS NEW. On 21 August President Masoud Pezeshkian said it is time to end the war while Tehran negotiates from a position of strength, and defended the 17 June memorandum of understanding with Washington against hardline critics in parliament - 'they cannot find even a single clause in this agreement that indicates capitulation'. The 60-day negotiating clock inside that memorandum expired on 17 August; the memorandum itself has not.

WHAT THE PHYSICAL PICTURE SAYS. Brent settled at $94.39 on 21 August, up about 6.4% over two weeks, while the US military says it has escorted more than 660m barrels of crude through the Strait of Hormuz since early May. The chokepoint is functioning and the premium is a risk premium rather than a supply outage.

AND IRAN AND OMAN HAVE NAMED A ROUTE. Bloomberg reported on 25-26 August that the two sides have agreed the geographic coordinates of a temporary, interim two-way shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz - a materially more specific de-escalation than the vaguer 'Hormuz management' talk this driver has previously declined to adopt. It is a negotiation over an existing arrangement, not yet an executed reopening: Iran's central bank governor still says the country's own oil exports are zero, and Gulf producers keep shipping.

investible_themes.read: NVIDIA IS PAYING ITS SUPPLY CHAIN TO BUILD WHAT IT NEEDS, AND THE STRUCTURE IS THE STORY. Nvidia is taking $3.5bn of MediaTek's $3.9bn overseas convertible bond - about 90% of the largest such offering in Taiwan's capital market history, and its largest direct investment outside the United States (Bloomberg, Reuters, Digitimes, 31 August). The stated purpose is custom silicon for AI companies and hyperscalers that plugs directly into Nvidia-based data centres, plus personal computing and vehicles; MediaTek rose about 10% on 1 September. It is the same instrument as the $2.0bn of convertible preferred stock Nvidia took in Marvell, completed 31 March and disclosed in Marvell's own 10-Q - a transaction that recirculated as fresh news last week and was five months old. Financing a supplier with a convertible keeps the ecosystem closed, moves capital intensity onto the balance sheet of the company that already sets the standard, and gives the buyer an equity claim on the value it creates. The foundry's own commitments this week were about packaging rather than price: a TSMC vice-president told SEMICON Taiwan that silicon photonics penetration passes 50% in 2027 with co-packaged optics mass production beginning in the second half, and the company set out an upgraded 3DFabric platform with CoWoS-integrated transistor volume projected to grow roughly 48 times by 2029. The 2027 wafer price increases reported on 30 August - 5% to 10% across advanced nodes, up to 10% on mature ones and a 10% to 15% surcharge above plan - remain supply-chain reporting rather than a company statement, and are carried as such against Bank of America's estimate of up to $85bn of 2027 capital spending. The supply-chain risk moved too: a Chinese court froze $300m of Nexperia's assets in the Wingtech case.

audit.note: Two secondary consensus sets are carried side by side rather than reconciled, because they disagree threefold on earnings per share and no primary compilation was obtained. Publishing either as the consensus would repeat the failure of 22 August, where a widely quoted probability was carried without asking what it was the probability of.

The H200 reopening was absent from this record until the 23 August sweep, despite being dated 19-20 August and carried by the FT, Tom's Hardware, Engadget and Benzinga. It is the second consecutive coverage gap traced to a scheduled or corporate event that no domain query was watching for.

The January 2026 licensing framework's 25% surcharge was absent from this record until today, as was the tension between shipments arriving on 19-20 August and a presidential statement that Beijing has approved nothing. The second is undated and is carried rather than used.

The undated Trump/H200 remark carried since 24 August as unresolved is now dated: 15 May 2026, following the Xi summit. It predates the framework's own shipments by three months and is consistent with them rather than contradicting them.
The 26 August print closes the largest outstanding open question carried since 19 August. It is read from the company's own release and the 8-K exhibit rather than from coverage of them.

The 27 August entry recorded Nvidia's reaction as '+4.4% after hours'. That was the extended-session print; the settled session on 27 August closed +9.1%. The snapshot understated the outcome by more than half, which is the same failure class as the Brent, Korea and gold errors and the first time it has run in this direction.

The $2bn Nvidia investment in Marvell closed as a trace on 31 August as real and five months old. The MediaTek convertible is a separate and new transaction, dated 31 August to Bloomberg and Reuters, and the reason both are recorded together is that the instrument is the same: a convertible into a supplier, not an acquisition.

investible_themes.glance: The company that sets the standard is now financing the suppliers who build to it, and the instrument is always a convertible.

investible_themes.read: A SECOND SETTLED SESSION HAS GONE AGAINST THE METAL FOR THE SAME REASON, AND THE MONTH STILL FINISHED STRONG. Gold settled $4,431.10 on Monday 31 August, down 1.05% on Friday's $4,478.10, and traded about $4,493 on Tuesday morning. The cause is unchanged from Friday and it is not a change in the physical case: futures moved to a 66% chance of a September Federal Reserve increase from a near-70% chance of no change before the Jackson Hole keynote, the ten-year settled at a nineteen-month high of 4.758%, and a metal that pays nothing is harder to hold against a rising real yield. That is now two settled sessions in which the rate path has beaten the official bid, after four earlier reads in which gold shrugged off hawkish news. The structural floor is intact and is what stops this being a break rather than a setback: record second-quarter official buying of 289 tonnes worth about $47.4bn, twenty consecutive months of Chinese accumulation totalling 2,346 tonnes, and record first-quarter producer margins despite costs up 16%. The level sits 20.8% below the $5,597.23 peak of 29 January 2026 and roughly 11% above where it started August, which was the best month since January. Goldman Sachs holds an end-2026 target of $4,900, JPMorgan about 30% higher and UBS above $5,400; none of the three is treated as evidence here.

The all-time high is now pinned to $5,597.23 on 29 January 2026 from a third independent source, narrowing the ~$5,589-5,602 band this record has carried since 17 August. The dated call of 14 July was formally assessed today as right, forty-one days on and +17.3%.

The two are deliberately different readings: the official bid is structural and was at a record last quarter, while the rate path is cyclical and turned against the metal in a single session. A 3% fall on a speech does not weaken a case built on sovereign buying, but it does end the run of the metal absorbing hawkish news without moving.

The 28 August settle recorded here yesterday, $4,529.90, was a provisional point that the source has since finalised at $4,478.10. Preferring a multi-point series over a lone quote remains right; preferring it over a lone quote while the series' final point is still provisional is not the same thing, and that distinction had not been drawn before.

The 31 August formal score recorded 28 August as the first settled session in which the rate path beat the official bid. Monday makes it two consecutive, which is the reason the characterisation moves from 'a session' to 'a pattern' while the score itself is not re-run - the next formal score is due 7 September on the flag's own age.

investible_themes.read: THE POWER QUEUE HAS A PHYSICAL BOTTLENECK AND THE NEWEST ENTRANT IS ATTACKING IT DIRECTLY. Elon Musk confirmed on 29 August that SpaceX is building a foundry in Bastrop, Texas to cast hot-section gas turbine blades and vanes - nickel-superalloy parts that run at 1,650 to 1,980 degrees, which only a handful of foundries worldwide can make and whose scarcity has pushed large-turbine delivery into 2030. The stated gain is up to eighteen months, and the same alloys and furnaces serve Raptor rocket-engine turbopumps, so one plant carries both businesses; SpaceX is separately sourcing three to four gigawatts of bridge power. This is a founder's statement and trade reporting rather than a company release, and it is carried on that basis. It sits alongside two other purchases of the constrained physical part in the same week: SLB agreed to buy Kelvion for $3.4bn, taking an oilfield services group into data-centre heat exchange, and Baker Hughes took an order for 76 gas turbines. On the regulatory side nothing has reversed - Delaware's legislation of 28 August stands as the fourth authority to decide that a large load pays for its own power, after PJM's FERC filing, the Georgia commission and Spain's hourly rule, and New Jersey's second-largest city has banned standalone data centres over bills. Siemens Energy confirmed the name it will trade under: Omterra unites the core business and Siemens Gamesa from later this year, ending about EUR 300m of annual licence fees, against a record EUR 162bn backlog and a EUR 10bn divestment drawing private equity bidders. The commercial answer still runs ahead of the rules, and Project Kilby's 2.67 gigawatts never connects at all.

investible_themes.read: TWO FACTS OF OPPOSITE SIGN LANDED ON THE SAME DAY. Samsung has committed roughly 70% of its memory production capacity to long-term agreements running to 2031, with Microsoft, Nvidia and Google named among the counterparties; inside those agreements a 36GB HBM3E module runs 500,000 to 700,000 Korean won against about 2.87m won on the spot market (Seoul Economic Daily, 31 August). Buyers signing five-year commitments at a fifth of spot are pricing a shortage that lasts rather than one that breaks, and contracted volume at a contracted price removes the sequential price rollover that would have broken this case - while also capping how much of a spot squeeze reaches the seller. Against that, China's ChangXin Memory Technologies has begun small-batch production of HBM3E, with Alibaba's T-Head and Cambricon testing it against their processors and commercial integration targeted for 2027. That is the substitution argument arriving on the ground this case actually rests on, four days after the LPDDR6 report which was mobile memory rather than high-bandwidth. The boundary is still real and still worth stating: HBM3E is one generation behind the HBM4 in mass production at Samsung, SK hynix and Micron, and reporting puts CXMT three to five years behind technically with low yields. Contracted demand is unchanged and enormous - Nvidia's disclosed supply commitments rose from $119bn to $279bn in a quarter, and TrendForce sizes DRAM and NAND at about 68% of major cloud providers' 2027 capital spending. Conventional prices set records again in August with the pace of gains slowing, spot HBM is reported at roughly five times contract levels, and Micron's Taiwanese unions have voted 80% in favour of a strike over bonuses. Micron's fiscal fourth quarter on 30 September is the next hard print.

The CXMT LPDDR6 claim carried as single-sourced yesterday is now corroborated across four independent trade outlets: CXMT has begun mass production at a 12,800 Mbps peak rate and up to 16GB, and the Xiaomi 18 Fold, launching in September, will be the first phone to ship it - ahead of Samsung and SK hynix, which have announced the standard but not shipped it commercially. Adopted as reported and corroborated rather than as a filed fact. It advances the named invalidation from a funded competitor to a shipped leading-edge part, but in mobile DRAM rather than in high-bandwidth memory or advanced packaging, which is where this case actually sits. Conviction held at 5 and the boundary stated rather than left implicit.

The 31 August boundary - that CXMT's advance was in mobile DRAM and not on this theme's ground - held for one day. The HBM3E report moves it onto the ground and the conviction is unchanged, because what moved is the timing of the substitution rather than its shape: small-batch output of a superseded generation being sampled is not commercial supply. The dated invalidation is restated as Chinese HBM at commercial volume ahead of the 2028-2030 base case.

investible_themes.read: THE FOUNDRY HAS DATED THE THING THIS THEME IS WAITING FOR. A TSMC vice-president told SEMICON Taiwan on 31 August that silicon photonics penetration passes 50% in 2027 and that co-packaged optics mass production begins in the second half of that year, alongside an upgraded 3DFabric platform in which CoWoS-integrated transistor volume is projected to grow roughly 48 times by 2029 (Taipei Times, Taiwan News, Focus Taiwan). Most of what this layer produces is trade commentary and market-size projections; a dated commitment from the company that has to build the packaging is a different class of evidence from a transceiver maker's outlook. It does not resolve the theme's central tension and in one sense sharpens it: the listed transceiver names capture this demand only while the optics stay on the board, and co-packaging is precisely the move that puts them inside the package, where the value accrues to the foundry and the switch vendor. The price and public-money legs recorded in late August stand - about $300m to GlobalFoundries for faster optical links between AI chips, Semtech up 10.17% on 26 August with data-centre revenue at $100m, and Lumentum and Coherent both higher the same day.

audit.note: The 22 August entry listed five August up-legs and no down-legs. Re-checking the same window returns a 10 August session in which Coherent fell 12% and Lumentum 7%. A price sweep looks for cluster moves, and cluster moves are reported asymmetrically to the upside, so the instrument that corrected a false silence carries a bias of its own. A year-to-date level is the sounder measure and is now carried. Separately, an 'AAOI plunges 17%' item that surfaced in the same search is dated 2 July and does not belong to the August window.

Trajectory cut flat to weakening: a second consecutive week of cluster declines is a level, not a run of headlines, and it is the standard this record adopted for itself on 23 August.

Applied Optoelectronics' continued fall since 21 August is not simply a continuation of the Fabrinet effect: an SEC 8-K dates a $600m at-the-market equity distribution agreement to 21 August, its third capital raise of the year, and the shares fell about 10% the same day on dilution rather than on mix.

Collection in this domain returned 62 items in a seven-day window, up from 51 and still fourth from bottom across the coverage universe. investible_themes.read: THE CONSTRAINT THIS CLUSTER HAS HAD ALL MONTH NOW HAS A STRUCTURAL ANSWER. The Department of War announced framework agreements with General Dynamics Ordnance and Tactical Systems and Lockheed Martin on 31 August, initiating seven-year multiyear procurement contracts intended to triple PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement output and quadruple THAAD interceptor output; General Dynamics expands motor cases, seeker housings, midsections and shroud deployment systems, and Lockheed separately holds a seven-year undefinitized contract action worth up to $35bn on THAAD announced 24 June. Orders have not been the problem in this theme since the spring - delivery has, with rebuilding depleted US missile stockpiles reported to need five years - and a seven-year framework is the first commitment long enough for a supplier to buy tooling against. The condition is in the release itself: funding remains subject to annual appropriations, and the appropriations deadline falls on 30 September. In Europe the disbursement story continues, with Romania having drawn its first EUR 2.5bn under the SAFE instrument and Italy formally requesting EUR 8bn, while Ukraine's defence minister seeks an early EU loan against a $27bn gap and Poland shifts toward domestic production as it builds Europe's largest army. The stage stays late: this is a well-owned trade with the order book already visible in the prices, and what has changed is the certainty of conversion rather than the size of the opportunity.

investible_themes.read: THE CONTROLS HAVE MOVED FROM THE MINE TO THE SCRAP HEAP. New US restrictions on tungsten and on battery 'black mass' are reported to be squeezing Chinese recyclers, who depend on imported feedstock to run the recycling capacity that has quietly become a large share of Chinese supply (South China Morning Post, 31 August). That is a different instrument from a mining or magnet restriction: it reaches a step in the chain that China had cornered without anyone legislating about it, and Shanghai Metals Market's own analysis describes ex-China scrap recycling moving from technology verification to locking in materials and customers. Four separate Western consolidations closed in the same week - Energy Fuels completed a $299m acquisition of an Australian metal producer to extend its mine-to-magnet chain, Mkango completed its purchase of Remloy, Neo Performance Materials partnered with Carester on European rare earth supply, and Astron received a US rare earth export licence - alongside $75m of funding for magnet recycling from waste. All of it says the same thing the Serra Verde price floor said on 27 August, when the Department of War committed $750m into a $1.55bn structure guaranteeing minimum prices of $2,050 a kilogram for terbium, $575 for dysprosium and $110 for neodymium-praseodymium: the West is building a parallel chain and is willing to pay above the market to have one. The equities have not followed - Energy Fuels, Aclara and Ucore all fell during the week - which is the gap between policy and price this theme has carried since it was created.

audit.note: The 22 August entry described the move as '+23.5% in the last week'. Against a dated close that is wrong: MP gained 2.26% over the week to 21 August and about 58% since 29 July. Two independent sources put the 21 August close within two cents of each other ($60.05 and $60.07), so the level is corroborated and only the window was mis-stated. Day-change figures differ between sources (+5% and +9.14%) and neither is adopted.

Momentum moves to flat. This record has read the export controls as a one-directional pull; the same week produced a measurement that they bind, a measurement that they are loosening for the United States, and a western price falling below its own floor. Averaging the three into one arrow would hide all of it.

MP's 25 August pullback to $57.66 is recorded as a level, not a reversal of the two-sided case: the stock remains well above its 52-week low. The NdPr-below-floor finding is upgraded from one specialist source (Benchmark) to two independently converging assessors, and Lynas's FY26 result adds the first hard non-US comparator print corroborating real rare-earth pricing improvement even as MP's own shares eased.

The '$703m record revenue' figure carried as an open trace since 27 August is the US dollar translation of A$977.9m, not an Australian dollar figure. The currency basis is now pinned and the full result adopted.

A conviction upgrade from 4 to 5 was considered and declined, and the reasoning is recorded so a later run can score it. The case for raising is that a guaranteed floor price converts a commodity thesis into a contracted one and has now been used twice, on neodymium with MP Materials and on dysprosium and terbium here. The case against, which won, is that the floors sit under a single offtake, Brazil's government has not reciprocated on the government-to-government leg, and the structure was already in this record on 28 August - so raising today would move a score on corroboration rather than on new evidence.

investible_themes.includes: Commercial launch, satellites and payload operators.
investible_themes.read: EUROPE'S SECURE-SATELLITE PROGRAMME PLACED ITS FIRST BIG CONTRACT AND IT WENT TO A LISTED COMPANY. SES awarded OHB, the Bremen-listed builder, nearly EUR 1bn on 31 August to develop and build eighteen medium-earth-orbit platforms for IRIS2 - the first major award under the concession, whose implementation phase began on 6 August. Each platform carries about 15 kilowatts and weighs roughly 2.6 tonnes; first launches are expected in 2029 with service from 2030, inside a 348-satellite constellation whose 330-satellite low-orbit segment Eutelsat leads. Four days earlier the European Space Agency's EUR 543.6m of European Launcher Challenge contracts went entirely to private companies - Isar Aerospace, Rocket Factory Augsburg, which flies from SaxaVord in Shetland, and PLD Space. Both facts belong together and they are the shape of the opportunity: European sovereign money has a listed route on the satellite side and none at all on the launch side, and in both cases the revenue belongs to the next decade. On the listed US side the picture is unchanged. Rocket Lab holds a $2.36bn backlog and record quarterly revenue of $234m, won a $12m Space Force data-network contract, and sold Kepler Communications a dedicated Neutron flight - the first full-vehicle commercial sale for a rocket still awaiting its debut, which cuts against a re-dating rather than for one. Coverage continues to describe the first Neutron flight slipping toward 2027; the company's own words remain delivery to the pad in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The launch side is not - all three European Launcher Challenge winners are private - and the programme's first revenue lands in 2029-2030, so this is a decade-long order book rather than a near-term earnings route. audit.note: Space was carried at emerging, conviction 3, on a 'cadence rather than catalysts' read while its largest constituent had already published a quarter. SpaceX's first earnings report is dated 4 August 2026 and was carried by Axios, NPR, CNBC, CNN and Fortune; a search of the ledger returns no hit for Starlink, for the $7.81bn revenue figure or for CFO Bret Johnsen. The 13F sweep of 19 August did record institutions adding to SpaceX, so the flows leg was checked and the print was not. Promoted to building at conviction 4 and given access routes on that basis.

The Iridium acquisition has been a matter of record since 29 June and was absent from the assessment until 23 August, while Rocket Lab sat on its expression line and its launch cadence was tracked week by week. Same cause as the SpaceX print found the day before: the corporate calendar of a named constituent was never a swept object.

The two Space Force awards read as this week's news across at least six outlets and are dated 27 July and 4 August. The undated-claims practice caught a fourth apparent fresh catalyst that was stale - and this time the same check surfaced the fact that mattered more, which is that the larger award depends on Neutron.

RKLB's price field is corrected from a stale 24 August rebound read (~$83, 'heading for its best month') to the current level: roughly $67-70 as of 25 August, about 55% below the 27 May high. The order-book evidence is unchanged and strong; the trajectory is written as two legs rather than one arrow because they now point in different directions.

The Neutron tank-test failure carried as unadopted since 26 August resolves to a hydrostatic pressure test on 21 January 2026 at the Maryland facility, attributed to a manufacturing fault. It caused the original slip to the fourth quarter, not this week's narrowing of the launch window, which comes from the chief executive's second-quarter remarks. Two events, several months apart.

Coverage on 26 August headlined that Neutron's first launch may slip to 2027. Read to the source, that is an inference from Beck's own statement - delivery to the pad targeted for Q4 2026, followed by pad testing including a first-stage static fire - rather than a company re-dating. Recorded as a narrowing window, not as a triggered kill, and carried as a trace.

investible_themes.read: THE MONEY CAME BACK WHILE THE STATUTE WENT THE OTHER WAY. US spot bitcoin funds took about $3.2bn over the week to 31 August, their best since October, before a $202m outflow day; ether funds added $60m in a session and XRP funds have passed $1.6bn of cumulative inflows. Bitcoin near $79,000 is doing this against a rising real yield and a two-thirds probability of a Federal Reserve increase, which is the part that is genuinely new - the correlation that has defined this asset since 2022 is not holding this month. The rulebook is moving in the opposite direction and is now splitting by geography. The Senate procedural vote on the CLARITY Act is set for 15 September and prediction-market traders price it at roughly a 14% chance; the US Treasury has proposed a GENIUS Act change requiring American exchanges to audit foreign stablecoin issuers or delist them; the Bank for International Settlements said stablecoins are not ready for everyday payment use and the IMF warned they threaten monetary sovereignty in emerging markets. Against that, the Bank of England's deputy governor signalled easier sterling stablecoin rules and Singapore proposed a regime covering foreign issuers and interest. The rails keep being built by banks and states rather than by Congress: Florida was the first state to pass a stablecoin bill, thirty-nine US banking groups are building a shared chain due in 2027, and Tether has launched a US-focused dollar token.

investible_themes.read: THE PREMIUM HAS FINISHED ITS MOVE OUT OF CRUDE AND INTO GAS, AND THIS WEEK SEPARATED THE TWO CLEANLY. US forces struck two rocket launchers on Iran's Larak Island on 30 August, the first publicly acknowledged strike since late July, and Iranian state media reported retaliation against US bases in Jordan. Brent settled $90.49 on Monday and was back near $88.5 on Tuesday morning as Washington signalled possible sanctions easing. Gas did not give anything back: the Dutch TTF front-month contract reached an intraday high of EUR 70.49 a megawatt-hour on 31 August, its highest since January 2023, with European storage 63% full in the final week of August - well below the seasonal average, in the middle of the refill season - and Goldman Sachs has said a sustained Gulf disruption forcing European buyers to outbid Asia could carry prices toward EUR 100. The asymmetry is physical rather than sentimental, and it is why the centre of gravity here is now European industrial cost rather than the oil price. The transmission has already reached a third region: European restocking is bidding cargoes away from Asia and has lifted South Korean power prices. Freight remains extraordinary, with very large crude carriers on the Gulf-to-China route assessed at a record $647,000 a day. US strategic reserves are reported at their lowest since 1982, and QatarEnergy's force majeure is reported extended into November against the October extension corroborated on 28 August, and that longer extension still rests on a single outlet.

audit.note: The 21 August score for this theme was partly withdrawn on 22 August once the reaction-function leg was found to rest on an inverted probability. What replaces it is a cleaner test: the premium is no longer transmitting into new markets, so it is measured by whether it holds. Two dated and opposing inputs now sit either side of it, one on 20 August and one on 21 August, and the 24 August package resolves the first of them.

European gas and LNG had never appeared in this record. The transmission the assessment was created to follow now runs through a physical shortage of winter storage in Europe, not only through crude and the long end, and that leg was absent for the entire period the record was rated at its highest conviction.

The 24 August sanctions announcement is the first genuine escalation in the history that did not move price in the expected direction. Recorded as a watch item against the high-conviction call rather than smoothed into the existing narrative - the entry stays confirmed/high on the strength of the gas leg, which is unaffected.

Conviction cut 5 to 4. Three consecutive down sessions in Brent, on a softer-than-threatened US sanctions round and specific, coordinate-level Iran-Oman corridor talks, is a materially different fact pattern from the single-day fade this record absorbed on 25 August without a score change. The entry's stated invalidation - an actual Hormuz reopening or blockade lift - has not triggered; this is recorded as a genuine two-sided challenge to a high-conviction call rather than smoothed into the standing narrative. The European gas leg is untouched by this and keeps the entry at confirmed rather than at risk of a stage change.

The two legs are now diverging enough that a single conviction number over both understates the gas side and overstates the crude side. Recorded here rather than acted on; splitting the entry would need the gas leg to have an investible basket distinct from the integrated majors, which it does not yet.

The 27 August entry described a fourth consecutive Brent fall to $86.43. That was the 06:00Z point on a 24-hour market; the settled 27 August close was $89.70, about 2% higher on the session, and same-day coverage put Brent near $90. The direction published was the opposite of the session's outcome. Same failure class as the Brent, Korea and gold errors already logged; the settled series is the anchor.

Sector momentum moved from flat to improving on the gas leg alone. The storage number, the force-majeure extension and the EUR 41bn cost estimate are three separate dated facts pointing the same way, against a crude leg that fell 4.35% on the week. The prior '~62%, lowest in nearly two decades' framing overstated the comparison by seven years and is corrected here rather than quietly replaced.

The 28 August settle recorded here yesterday, $88.10, was a provisional point the source has since finalised at $89.31. The day change becomes -0.43% rather than -1.78% and the week -5.38% rather than -6.66%. Today's tile change of +1.40% reconciles exactly against $89.31 as the prior point. The direction was right in both versions; the magnitude of the daily fall was overstated fourfold. Same new class as the gold correction logged today: a provisional Friday point carried on a weekend run.

The 31 August entry said the premium had transmitted to a third region through gas rather than crude. This week separates the two legs with a dated price on each: crude round-tripped its war premium inside twenty-four hours and gas set a three-and-a-half-year high on the same news.

investible_themes.read: A RESTART REACHED FUEL, WHICH IS THE STEP THAT MAKES IT REAL. Holtec announced the start of fuel loading at the Palisades plant in Michigan, the furthest any shut American reactor has come on the way back to generation (NucNet, 31 August). Restarts have been the cheapest gigawatts in the American power argument for a year, and until now the evidence was permits and financing rather than fuel. The appropriated money recorded on 26 August continues to disburse: the US Army's Janus programme committed up to $2.2bn through fiscal 2031 across five vendors and five bases for more than twenty commercial microreactors, and Radiant's share of it is reported at $750m by a single outlet, and is not treated as established until the vendor figure and the programme figure are reconciled. The week's other purchase says where the constraint actually is: SLB agreed to buy Kelvion for $3.4bn, taking an oilfield services group into data-centre heat exchange. American uranium output has tripled and still does not cover domestic reactor demand. Of the five named Janus vendors only some are directly listed, which remains the reason the cleanest exposure here runs through fuel and through the utilities rather than through the reactor builders.

audit.note: Third consecutive cycle without a fresh dated catalyst, and the first in which the cluster's price tape was checked before the finding was recorded. That check went the opposite way to the optics and rare-earth checks of 22 August: those found a live tape behind a quiet news feed, this found a deep drawdown behind a calm assessment. The only recent apparent catalyst, the Centrus-Oklo HALEU letter of intent, is dated 18 June. Conviction 4 to 3.

Momentum moves from deteriorating to flat. The 23 August cut rested on price and revenue at the reactor developers and that finding is unchanged; what was missing is that the fuel cycle signed four separate dated agreements in the same week, and those are different companies with different economics.

The Westinghouse IPO already referenced via the Cameco access route is now independently dated: a confidential S-1 draft was submitted to the SEC on 31 July 2026, with share terms not yet set. The 25 August bounce in reactor-developer equities is recorded as a bounce off a deep drawdown, not as a change to the 23 August conviction cut, which rested on price and revenue at the developers rather than on sentiment.

Conviction raised 3 to 4. The entry's stated weakness was that contracts were reaching the fuel cycle and losses were sitting in the reactor developers. The Janus awards put appropriated money directly on reactor builders through fiscal 2031, with BWX Technologies and Westinghouse among the five named.

Conviction held at 4 on the strongest single week the record shows. investible_themes.read: THE APPROVALS ARE IN AUTONOMY AND THE EVIDENCE IN HUMANOIDS IS STILL SECOND-HAND. Tesla's Cybercab production event falls on 3 September and is the nearest dated test. Against that, a Waymo executive publicly argued that camera-only self-driving cannot see enough, which is the technical dispute the whole revenue case turns on. In humanoids the week produced a number and it came from the wrong kind of source: Digitimes reports shipments topping 22,000 in the first half of 2026 with industrial use gaining ground, and Europe's first humanoid mass-production base began output in a China-Serbia joint venture. A trade research house counting shipments is not a maker disclosing deployments, and the difference is the whole question of whether these machines are working or merely being built. The London rollout still waits on guidance. Conviction holds at 3: the revenue and the regulatory permission are in autonomy, and the humanoid leg remains a set of announcements about capacity rather than about work done.

Held on the radar at a full five of five for a further run, and the reason is now written into the entry rather than left implicit. radar.summ: The expression is being punished by exactly the macro that would have to turn for the thesis to work. The aggregate American labour market still is not turning - Warsh's own reading is that it is at full employment - while the entry-level market weakens: employment among 22-to-25-year-olds in highly AI-exposed occupations was running about 19% behind less-exposed peers by June 2026, and the count of the functionally unemployed is climbing while the official rate falls. radar.needs: A second soft US payroll on 4 September alongside rising continuing claims, and a policy path that is not arguing about a rise. The deeper problem is unchanged and has worsened: long-duration Treasuries express a rate cut, and every week that the September argument moves further toward a rise costs this expression money while the underlying labour thesis is untested.

radar.what: Payment-stablecoin issuance, settlement and merchant plumbing - the layer the GENIUS Act governs, distinct from the listed asset complex.
radar.summ: The rulebook is now splitting by geography rather than simply advancing. Tether has launched a US-focused token. The rails keep being built by banks and states while the federal statute stalls.
radar.needs: Final rules rather than proposals, and a listed way to own the issuance layer. That has not changed, and the geographic split makes it harder rather than easier: a British easing and an American tightening pull the economics of a single global issuer in opposite directions, and the largest issuers remain private.

radar.what: Magnetic, inertial and magneto-inertial fusion developers, and the pulsed-power and magnet supply chain behind them.
radar.summ: A state has written a rulebook for fusion and then used it. Tennessee's environment department, with Governor Bill Lee, issued the first fusion-specific byproduct material licence in the United States to Type One Energy on 30-31 August, under the first state fusion regulatory framework in the country, which took effect on 9 June 2026. It covers Project Infinity at the Tennessee Valley Authority's Bull Run complex in Clinton, developed with Oak Ridge National Laboratory and the University of Tennessee: a prototype commissioning in 2029, and a 400 megawatt stellarator whose construction could begin in 2028 with full startup expected by 2034. Separately, Helical Fusion was named a final candidate for Japan's METI fusion demonstration programme. The stated obstacle to this field has always been that no regulator had a category for it, and one now does.
radar.needs: More than one listed name, so that a basket exists rather than a single pre-revenue ticker; a demonstrated net-energy milestone rather than a temperature or a licence milestone; and evidence that the capital reaching this field is arriving faster than the schedules are slipping. Type One Energy is private and its own timeline runs to 2034, so the licence changes the regulatory risk rather than the access problem.
