A widely circulated 24 August item describing Germany's 'plans for Europe's first commercial fusion plant' recycles a funding decision Germany's BMFTR actually made on 6 August (EUR 125m federal plus EUR 400m Bavaria for three fusion R&D hubs) - not adopted as a fresh catalyst. This domain's own collected-item count remains far thinner than every other tracked domain, a collection gap rather than a true quiet signal.

A '$4bn raised' figure circulating this week (25 Aug) restates, rather than adds to, the $1bn tranche that closed 30 July and brought Commonwealth Fusion's cumulative total to $3.94-4bn - not adopted as fresh capital flow. A DOE fusion roadmap recirculating the same day was finalised well before this window and is similarly not new. TAE/Trump Media confirmed still targeting a Q4 2026 merger close; the media-asset spin-off evaluated alongside it has been shelved. Collection breadth improved to 18 items this week (from 9-13 the prior two runs) but remains the thinnest domain tracked.
The widely shared '$4bn raised' Commonwealth Fusion headline recirculating this week restates a 30 July close and is not new money. Not counted, for a second consecutive cycle.

Held at 3 of 5. A memorandum with a listed utility is a counterparty rather than a contract and does not move the access criterion. The 'CFS raises $4bn' item circulating in this domain was traced to a 30 July release stating cumulative capital; it is a restatement outside the week and is not counted.

The domain returned 16 items in seven days, a sixth consecutive thin sample, and still produced the strongest single item this entry has carried. That is the argument against inferring silence from volume: a small sample is not the same as a quiet field.

radar.what: Individualised and computationally designed therapeutics - neoantigen vaccines, AI-designed molecules and the sequencing and manufacturing behind them.
radar.summ: Nothing changed the case this week and very little happened at all. The strongest item in the field was a single small-cap holding steady ahead of licensing milestones. The standing evidence is unchanged: Merck and Moderna's phase 3 INTerpath-001 readout of intismeran autogene on 19 August still stands as the late-stage datapoint, and no approval or filing for an individualised therapy has followed it. One adjacent item is worth recording rather than adopting - DualityBio and Genentech signed an antibody-drug conjugate partnership worth more than $1bn - because it is computational design money arriving in a conventional modality.
radar.needs: An approval or a filing for an individualised therapy rather than a readout, a second sponsor reaching phase 3 on the same approach, and a listed basket that is not two large-cap pharmaceutical companies. None moved.
evidence: Merck and Moderna: phase 3 INTerpath-001 met RFS and DMFS endpoints for intismeran autogene plus pembrolizumab in resected stage IIB-IV melanoma (19 Aug 2026)
1,137 patients randomised 2:1; the therapy encodes up to 34 patient-specific neoantigens; supported by KEYNOTE-942 five-year data

Moderna spiked +177% intraday on 19 Aug, gave back ~20-25% the next session on profit-taking, and closed 25 Aug at $156.75 - still roughly 2.5x its pre-announcement level; Merck rose 12.5% on 19 Aug and traded 24 Aug within ~1% of a fresh 52-week high ($152.85); BioNTech closed 19 Aug near $112, up roughly 20-24% from its base; Tempus AI added ~$3bn on its Personalis stake
FDA approved an Ultragenyx gene therapy (20 Aug) - a separate approval in the same individualised-medicine window
Isomorphic Labs has raised $2.1bn with no disclosed clinical candidate as of mid-2026
The FDA is expected to finalise AI-in-drug-development guidance during 2026

FDA approved Revolution Medicines' Rasonque (daraxonrasib) on 26 Aug, the first targeted therapy for metastatic pancreatic cancer - median overall survival 13.2 months in the second line against 6.7 on chemotherapy. Recorded as adjacent; not scored into this basket pending confirmation of whether the molecule was computationally designed

The FDA approved the first targeted therapy for metastatic pancreatic cancer (STAT, 26 Aug). It stays adjacent to this basket and is not counted: the molecule was found by structure-guided optimisation from a natural-product scaffold, which is medicinal chemistry rather than computational design

2026-08-31 DualityBio and Genentech partnered on next-generation antibody-drug conjugates in a deal worth more than $1bn (BioSpectrum Asia) - recorded as adjacent, not as evidence for individualised medicine.
2026-09-01 The biotech domain returned 13 items in seven days, a FOURTH consecutive record low. Absence recorded on a measured sample; the sample itself is the finding.

audit.note: The 23 August 01:00 sweep recorded this domain as thin, on a single negative datapoint, while the largest possible catalyst for it had printed on 19 August and was carried by the trade press. That is a false silence of the same class as water and rare earths, and its cause is the same: too few observations to filter. It is the clearest single argument in this run's evidence for separating collection from judgement.

Twenty-four collected items across the week and the picture is unchanged from 23 August: the readout is the whole story and the follow-through is a filing that has not happened. Fierce Biotech frames the result as setting up an approval push, which is the next milestone this item names.

The price-leg evidence materially understated the actual move: Moderna's real reaction was a 177% intraday spike and a partial reversal, not a flat +8%, and Merck's sustained level (within 1% of a 52-week high five sessions later) is a stronger signal-1 confirmation than previously credited. Neither the filing/approval criterion nor the second-sponsor-at-phase-3 criterion is met - BioNTech's own comparable candidate, autogene cevumeran, remains in Phase 2 - so the score stays at 2 of 5 despite the corrected, stronger price evidence.

The approval arrived and the exclusion decided on 28 August holds unchanged. Recorded explicitly so a later run does not read the approval as evidence for the assessment, which is the obvious mistake to make with it.

The biotech domain returned 13 items in a seven-day window, a fourth consecutive record low against a store of 5,908 items across 34 domains. Absence is recorded on a measured sample rather than inferred, and the sample size is itself escalated to the collector's owner as a breadth defect.

radar.what: On-device inference silicon and the robotics/consumer hardware built on it.
radar.needs: A design win disclosed by a CUSTOMER in its own filing or release rather than through the supplier's press channel, evidence that the named partners are shipping rather than supporting, and a pure-play basket that does not resolve to the same handful of large-cap silicon names. The first is now nearly met and the distinction being held is the difference between a press release and a disclosure.
evidence: NVIDIA launched the Jetson Orin Nano 2 edge-AI robotics computer via its own newsroom on 25 Aug 2026 (78 TOPS, 8GB, 2x inference performance, 40% lower power than its predecessor)
Named launch-day partners: Cognex confirmed support the same day; Aptiv announced production-ready physical-AI support for the same chip on 25 Aug
Apple launched M6/M5 Max/M5 Ultra chips on 25 Aug 2026 (Apple Newsroom), framed explicitly around AI compute; new Mac Studio and Mac mini pre-orders opened 25 Aug, shipping 22 Sept 2026

This revives a flag that fired 18 Aug and was confirmed quiet for nine consecutive cycles - the two 25 August launches are the first primary-sourced, dated, named-beneficiary product launches to meet the flag's own stated revival bar since it fired

Apple shipped its first 2nm chip and AWS and Nvidia expanded their infrastructure partnership (26 Aug); Qualcomm released IMSDK 2.0 for accelerated edge AI. Samsung is reported to be moving AI compute into DRAM with a drop-in part that triples inference - single trade source, logged not scored

Samsung presented LPDDR5X-PIM at Hot Chips on 25 August: 3.01x the AI token throughput of standard LPDDR5X and 614 GB/s inside the same 561-ball package, tripling Llama 3.1 throughput from 27 to 81.3 tokens per second. A conference presentation with no availability date - and the most consequential on-device inference datapoint this entry has recorded
Intel detailed Diamond Rapids at 256 cores and Crescent Island with 480GB aimed at inference (Hot Chips, 24-25 Aug); Xiaomi's Xring O3 is the first phone processor with LPDDR6

2026-08-31 Express LUCK selected MemryX for AI-enabled smart manufacturing operations and MemryX announced an edge AI deployment in global television manufacturing (PR Newswire, TipRanks) - the closest this entry has come to a customer-side design win, still issued through the supplier's channel with no order value.

2026-09-01 DeepX linked its NPU to AWS to scale edge AI, targeting US robotics and factories (Chosunbiz); Microchip shrank its PolarFire ethernet sensor bridge for edge AI systems (EE Times Asia, 31 Aug).
radar.summ: A customer named a vendor for the first time in weeks, and it came through the vendor's own channel. Express LUCK selected MemryX for AI-enabled smart manufacturing and MemryX announced a deployment in global television manufacturing; DeepX linked its neural processing unit to AWS to scale edge AI toward US robotics and factories; Microchip shrank its PolarFire ethernet sensor bridge for edge systems. That is closer to the shape this entry needs than the vendor launches it has been recording all month, and it still arrives as a press release rather than as a customer disclosure or a disclosed order value.

audit.note: 137 items in a seven-day window. The MemryX items are the closest this record has come to a customer-side design win in seven cycles, and they are still issued through the supplier's press channel with no disclosed order value - which is why the assessment moves and the score does not.

radar.what: Regulated and offshore venues trading binary contracts on events - elections, sport, macro prints - and the exchanges, brokers and clearing that carry them.
radar.summ: A sector that has roughly quadrupled in private value inside a year has just had its central premise moved into litigation, and the two facts are three days apart. On 28 August the Ninth Circuit denied Kalshi, Crypto.com and Robinhood injunctions against the Nevada Gaming Control Board, holding sports event contracts are likely bets rather than federally regulated swaps and that commodities law probably does not preempt state gaming rules - contradicting a Third Circuit ruling and creating a circuit split, with traders now pricing a 52% chance the Supreme Court takes the case. British Columbia's regulator has reached the same view as Nevada and Kentucky has sued. On 31 August 1789 Capital led a $1bn round valuing Polymarket at $21bn post-money, up from $15bn in April; Intercontinental Exchange completed a $1.6bn investment earlier this year and Kalshi was valued at $22bn in May. Kalshi has taken an exclusive US Open deal and partnered with Alpaca for global expansion; Polymarket says its surveillance systems are ready for the US midterms.
radar.needs: A listed way to own the venues rather than their landlords - both leaders are private, so the only routes today are the exchange and brokerage owners, where the revenue is diluted to invisibility. Beyond that: a resolution of the circuit split, since the entire valuation rests on whether federal registration displaces state gambling law; and evidence that volumes hold outside an election cycle. Sell-side coverage does not meaningfully exist and there is no cohort to measure a price leg across.
evidence: 2026-08-28 The Ninth Circuit denied Kalshi, Crypto.com and Robinhood injunctions against the Nevada Gaming Control Board, holding sports event contracts are likely bets and that commodities law probably does not preempt state gaming rules (CNBC, The Hill, CoinDesk, Sportico) - contradicting a Third Circuit ruling and creating a circuit split.

2026-08-31 1789 Capital led a $1bn round valuing Polymarket at $21bn post-money, up from $15bn in April; Intercontinental Exchange completed a $1.6bn investment this year; Kalshi was valued at $22bn in May (Bloomberg, PYMNTS).

2026-08-31 Traders put a 52% chance on the Supreme Court taking the Kalshi case (sccgmanagement, iGamingToday); British Columbia's regulator declared prediction market trading to be gambling (Iredell Free News); Kalshi took an exclusive US Open prediction market deal and partnered with Alpaca for global expansion (CoinMarketCap, streamlinefeed).
radar.eta: 12-24 months, gated on the circuit split

audit.note: Opened as a new radar entry rather than folded into the crypto or capital-markets records. The subject is distinct from both: it is neither a digital asset nor an equity listing pipeline, its regulator is a state gaming board rather than the SEC or CFTC alone, and the two largest venues are private - which is the condition that puts a subject on the radar rather than in the book.

retired.why: The exit thesis was wrong. Bitcoin broke out and its leveraged equity proxy amplified the move, which is exactly what the flag said would not happen.
retired.callTxt: Wrong, against a dated close rather than a feeling. The exit call was $91.39 on 14 July; the equity closed $112.39 on 20 August, +23.0% against it. The call was written to fail if bitcoin passed $70,000 or the equity passed $110, and the equity leg went through on a settled session close.
retired.reviveIf: Not a revival condition but a lesson: the call was written on a leveraged proxy while the underlying was the actual variable, and it ran through four cycles in which its level could not be pinned. Judge a proxy against the thing it proxies, and close a call whose level cannot be sourced rather than deriving one.

audit.note: The bitcoin leg was deliberately not used on 21 August because the last settled close available then was $69,266.19, 1.1% below the trigger, with only an in-progress snapshot above it. The settled 21 August point is $78,335.19, so that leg has since triggered decisively and the call is unchanged - the caution cost nothing.

Two separable lessons. The flag was written on a leveraged proxy while the underlying was the actual variable, so the equity amplified an 11% move in bitcoin exactly as designed. And it consumed five runs on the single question of what its level was; a flag whose level cannot be sourced in two consecutive runs is now closed rather than carried.
Renamed. The record and its lesson stay; the single-name flag naming does not, because the page tracks themes rather than tickers and the old name is why this was hidden from readers.

retired.why: The exit thesis inverted — memory became the cleanest confirmed recipient of AI capex, not a fade.
retired.callTxt: Wrong on thesis. The memory exit call inverted: memory became the cleanest confirmed recipient of AI capital spending rather than a fade. Retired 10 August and kept in the record for the lesson.
retired.reviveIf: A DRAM/HBM ASP sequential rollover, or CXMT reaching HBM-capable output ahead of the 2028–30 base case.

audit.note: Renamed for the same reason as the bitcoin-proxy call. The condition it named - a sequential fall in average selling prices, or CXMT reaching high-bandwidth output early - remains the live test on the memory theme, and CXMT moved closer on the performance axis this week.

The private side is drying rather than merely silent - the median 2026 round is about $12m and the year's two largest, Halter at $220m and Tropic at $105m, are both dated March.

101 items read and nothing met the bar. One small named round, Mafix at $5.4m for silicate-rock fertiliser, is the whole week.

The two listed names moved apart rather than together - Lincoln Educational Services adding a twenty-sixth campus while Universal Technical Institute cut full-year revenue guidance to $893-900m from $905-915m - and no third name emerged to make a basket. The subject also has no queries in the collection that feeds this page, so its position was carried rather than refreshed for six consecutive cycles. Parking it is more honest than carrying an entry that cannot be checked.

The entry had been recorded as stalled for six runs while the collection that feeds this page holds no queries for the subject, so 'stalled' described the gathering rather than the theme. Carrying an unobservable entry makes the radar look fuller than it is.

signals.headline: China's private factory gauge recorded its longest run of expansion in five years while the official one stayed in contraction
summary: The private survey beat forecasts on 1 September and marked the longest expansion in five years.
The official gauge improved in August but stayed below the expansion line, with new orders rebounding and employment still shrinking.
Shein's Hong Kong debut fell on its first day; Vietnam's FTSE emerging-market upgrade took effect.
signals.assessment: The two surveys have disagreed for months and the gap is the finding: the private sample skews to smaller exporters, so a five-year high there against contraction in the official series says the recovery is narrow. Employment shrinking through both is the reading that matters for the demand case.

signals.headline: Austal reported record revenue and a loss while Hanwha's exclusive look at its American yard runs out next week
signals.src: Investing.com transcript / The West Australian / TipRanks
summary: Austal posted record FY2026 revenue of about A$2bn with a statutory loss and an order book of A$16.5bn, and flagged a potential $1.67bn contract (31 August).
Hanwha has assembled a bid team for Austal USA; its four-week exclusive due diligence expires around 8 September.
China took 82.5% of global new ship orders in the first half of 2026, and the global orderbook stands at $666bn.
signals.assessment: The industrial policy is real and the profitability is not yet: a record top line with a loss under it is what a yard looks like while it is being rebuilt. The concentration figure is the reason the policy exists. What is still absent is anyone buying the shares: neither fund flows nor analyst coverage moved this week.

signals.headline: Palisades began loading fuel, the first American reactor restart to reach that step
summary: Holtec announced the start of fuel loading at the Palisades plant in Michigan, advancing toward the first restart of a shut US reactor.
SLB agreed to buy Kelvion for $3.4bn, extending an oilfield services company into data-centre heat exchange.
US uranium output has tripled but still does not cover domestic reactor demand.
signals.assessment: Restarts have been the cheapest gigawatts in the American power argument for a year and this is the first one to reach fuel. It also marks where the money now goes: an oilfield services group paying $3.4bn for heat exchangers is the same trade as a rocket company casting turbine blades - buying the constrained physical part rather than the headline generation.

signals.headline: Washington extended export controls to tungsten and battery black mass, squeezing Chinese recyclers
signals.src: South China Morning Post / Qatar Tribune / tippinsights
summary: New US controls on tungsten and on battery 'black mass' are reported to be pressuring Chinese recyclers, who depend on imported feedstock.

Separately, Energy Fuels closed a $299m acquisition of an Australian metal producer to extend its mine-to-magnet chain, Mkango completed its purchase of Remloy, and Neo Performance Materials partnered with Carester on European rare earth supply.
Astron received a US rare earth export licence.
signals.assessment: The instrument has widened from the mine to the scrap heap, which is the part of the chain China had cornered without anyone legislating about it. Four separate Western consolidations inside a week say the same thing the Serra Verde price floor said on 27 August: the West is building a parallel chain and is willing to pay above the market to have one.

signals.headline: An Australian property failure became the first real test of retail private credit, in the month the wrapper opened in Britain
summary: Bloomberg reported an Australian property collapse as the first real test for private credit funds in that market (31 August).
It lands alongside Apollo's redemption cap, imposed in June after exit requests reached 16.8%, and MA Financial's 1% monthly cap from 25 August.

In the same month the Financial Conduct Authority authorised the Legal and General and WTW private credit long-term asset fund for defined-contribution schemes, and Goldman Sachs began preparing a retail private equity fund.
signals.assessment: The access rail and the liquidity are still travelling in opposite directions and the gap has widened rather than closed. A saver reaching these assets through the newest wrapper meets the gate last rather than first, and the first genuine credit event in the asset class is now being watched in a market smaller than either Britain's or America's.

signals.headline: Bitcoin funds took $3.2bn in their best week since October while the enabling statute slipped toward a 15 September vote
summary: US spot bitcoin funds drew about $3.2bn over the week to 31 August, their strongest since October, before a $202m outflow day; ether funds added $60m in a single session.
The Senate procedural vote on the CLARITY Act is set for 15 September and prediction-market traders put its chances at about 14%.

Bank of England deputy governor signalled easier sterling stablecoin rules; the Treasury proposed a GENIUS Act change requiring US exchanges to audit foreign stablecoin issuers or delist them; the BIS said stablecoins are not ready for everyday payments and the IMF warned on emerging-market monetary sovereignty.
signals.assessment: Flows and rules are moving in opposite directions again, and the split is now geographic: Britain is loosening while Washington tightens the perimeter around foreign issuers and the enabling bill is priced to fail. Bitcoin near $79,000 is doing this against a rising real yield, which is the part that is genuinely new.

signals.headline: Tennessee issued the first US state licence for a commercial fusion plant
signals.src: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation / World Nuclear News / ANS
summary: Governor Bill Lee and the state environment department announced Tennessee's first fusion-specific byproduct material licence, issued to Type One Energy.
It is granted under the first state fusion regulatory framework in the country, which took effect on 9 June 2026.

The licence covers Project Infinity at the Tennessee Valley Authority's Bull Run complex in Clinton: a prototype commissioning in 2029 and a 400 megawatt stellarator whose construction could begin in 2028, with full startup expected by 2034.
signals.assessment: The strongest single item this domain has produced. Fusion's stated obstacle has been that no regulator had a category for it, and a state has now written one and used it. It does not create a basket - Type One Energy is private and the timeline runs to the 2030s - which is why this stays on the radar rather than moving.

signals.headline: Portugal and an Italian developer added a second and third public procurement leg to grid storage in a week
summary: Portugal opened a consultation on a strategy targeting 6.9 gigawatts of storage by 2030 (31 August).
Zhero signed an agreement with Tesla Energy for 3 gigawatt-hours of capacity in Italy (1 September).
Both follow SK On's 9 gigawatt-hour, roughly $1.09bn contract with NeoVolta Power confirmed by Reuters on 30 August.
signals.assessment: Three separate European and American procurement legs inside a week, and the American one is confirmed by a wire service. What is still absent is the flows and coverage evidence that would move this off the radar: buyers are visible, buyers of the equities are not.

signals.headline: September rate-increase odds reached 66% and the ten-year yield hit a nineteen-month high
summary: CME FedWatch put the odds of a September increase at 66.1% on Monday 31 August, roughly double where they sat before the Jackson Hole keynote, when a hold was near 70%.
The ten-year Treasury settled 4.758%, its highest in nineteen months; the dollar index settled 99.43.
Not all measures agree - one fed funds futures read was near 56% and Kalshi traders were at 48%. The decision is on 16 September.
signals.assessment: The repricing is now the dominant fact in the market. The dispersion between measures matters as much as the level: a market that has moved from a third to two thirds in three sessions is pricing a speech rather than a print, and Friday's employment report is the first hard evidence either way.

signals.headline: ECB analysts warned that American technology borrowing is raising European funding costs
summary: European Central Bank analysts said the scale of US technology issuance in the euro bond market could raise European borrowing costs.
A separate warning covered European pension funds buying into the American AI build and credit ratings that may understate future risk.
This is the same crowding-out effect fund managers described in Treasuries in late August, now measured on the other side of the Atlantic.
signals.assessment: The financing leg of the AI build has been the contested one all month, and until now the strain was described only in dollars. A European supervisor saying the issuance reaches euro-area funding costs makes it a transmission channel rather than a US market story, and it is the reason this driver stays at rising rather than flat.

signals.headline: Polymarket raised $1bn at a $21bn valuation three days after a court put its product back under state gambling law
summary: 1789 Capital led a $1bn round valuing Polymarket at $21bn post-money on 31 August, up from $15bn in April; Intercontinental Exchange completed a $1.6bn investment earlier this year.
Kalshi was valued at $22bn in May.

On 28 August the Ninth Circuit denied Kalshi, Crypto.com and Robinhood injunctions against Nevada, holding sports event contracts are likely bets rather than federally regulated swaps - contradicting a Third Circuit ruling and sending the question toward the Supreme Court.
signals.assessment: A sector that has roughly quadrupled in private value inside a year has just had its central premise - that federal registration settles the state gambling question - moved into litigation. Both facts are three days apart and both are dated. The purest exposure is private on both sides, so a reader's listed routes are the exchange and brokerage owners rather than the venues.

signals.headline: Europe's secure-satellite programme placed its first major contract and it went to a listed European builder
summary: SES awarded OHB, the Bremen-listed builder, nearly EUR 1bn on 31 August to develop and build 18 medium-earth-orbit platforms for IRIS2, the first major contract under the concession.
Each platform carries about 15 kilowatts and weighs roughly 2.6 tonnes; first launches are expected in 2029 with service from 2030.
IRIS2 totals 348 satellites - 18 in medium orbit led by SES, 330 in low orbit led by Eutelsat - and its implementation phase began on 6 August.
signals.assessment: Four days ago European sovereign launch money had no listed route at all, because all three European Launcher Challenge winners are private. The satellite side is different: this contract is with a company a European investor can buy, and it is the largest single award the programme has made. The delivery dates are late enough that the revenue belongs to the next decade.

signals.headline: SpaceX is building a turbine-blade foundry, going after the part of the power queue that money cannot shorten
summary: Musk confirmed on 29 August that SpaceX is casting hot-section turbine blades and vanes at a new foundry in Bastrop, Texas.

Only a handful of foundries worldwide can cast the nickel-superalloy parts that run at 1,650-1,980C, and the shortage has pushed large-turbine delivery into 2030; the stated gain is up to eighteen months.
The same alloys and furnaces serve Raptor rocket-engine turbopumps, so one plant carries both businesses.
signals.assessment: The constraint on data-centre power stopped being generation capacity some months ago and became castings, and this is the first attempt by a non-incumbent to build the constrained part rather than to queue for it. A founder's statement and trade reporting rather than a company release or a permit record, and carried on that basis.

signals.headline: TSMC put a date on co-packaged optics: more than half of its advanced packaging penetrated by 2027
signals.src: Taipei Times / Taiwan News / Focus Taiwan
summary: A TSMC vice-president told SEMICON Taiwan that silicon photonics penetration passes 50% in 2027 and that co-packaged optics mass production begins in the second half.
The company also set out an upgraded 3DFabric platform, with CoWoS-integrated transistor volume projected to grow roughly 48 times by 2029.
SEMICON Taiwan 2026 framed the interconnect between chips, rather than the chips themselves, as the bottleneck.
signals.assessment: Most of what this layer produces is trade commentary and market projections; this is a dated commitment from the company that has to build the packaging. It remains a schedule rather than a shipment, and the listed transceiver names capture the demand only if the optics stay on the board rather than moving inside the package - which is precisely what co-packaging changes.

signals.headline: The United States struck Iranian positions for the first time since late July and Tehran said it hit US bases in Jordan
summary: US forces struck two rocket launchers on Iran's Larak Island on Sunday 30 August, the first publicly acknowledged strike on Iranian positions since late July.
Iranian state media reported retaliatory attacks on US bases in Jordan.
Brent rose to about $90.5 and the S&P 500 fell 0.33% on Monday, while US crude gained more than 3%.
signals.assessment: Six months in, the conflict has settled into a pattern where each exchange moves energy first and equities second, and this one moved gas hardest of all. The market reaction was smaller than the headline: the index fell a third of a percent and still closed August higher.

signals.headline: European gas passed EUR 70 a megawatt-hour for the first time since January 2023
summary: The Dutch TTF front-month contract reached an intraday high of EUR 70.49 a megawatt-hour on 31 August, a three-and-a-half-year high, as renewed US-Iran fighting threatened Gulf liquefied natural gas exports.
European storage was 63% full in the final week of August, well below the seasonal average, during the refill season.
Goldman Sachs has said a sustained Gulf disruption that forces European buyers to outbid Asia could push prices toward EUR 100.
signals.assessment: The premium has completed its move out of crude and into gas. Brent settled $90.49 on Monday and was back near $88.5 the next morning on talk of sanctions easing, while gas set a three-year high on the same news - because a tanker can be re-routed and a liquefaction train cannot. Europe carries this one directly, through industrial costs and through the utility bill.

signals.headline: The Pentagon signed seven-year agreements to triple Patriot and quadruple THAAD interceptor production
signals.src: US Department of War (war.gov) / Defence Industry Europe / AeroTime
summary: The Department of War announced framework agreements with General Dynamics Ordnance and Tactical Systems and Lockheed Martin initiating seven-year multiyear procurement contracts (31 August).

The stated goals are to triple PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement output and quadruple Terminal High Altitude Area Defense interceptor output, with General Dynamics expanding motor cases, seeker housings, midsections and shroud deployment systems.
Lockheed separately holds a seven-year undefinitized contract action worth up to $35bn on THAAD, announced 24 June. Funding remains subject to annual appropriations.
signals.assessment: Delivery rather than orders has been the binding constraint in this cluster all month, and this is the first structural answer to it: a multiyear commitment long enough for a supplier to buy tooling against. The qualifier is in the release itself - the money is appropriated annually, so a seven-year framework is a plan, not a seven-year cheque, and the appropriations deadline is 30 September.

signals.headline: Nvidia put $3.5bn into MediaTek through convertible bonds, its largest direct investment outside the United States
summary: Nvidia is taking $3.5bn of MediaTek's $3.9bn overseas convertible bond, about 90% of the largest such offering in Taiwan's capital market history (31 August).
The stated purpose is custom silicon for AI companies and hyperscalers that plugs directly into Nvidia-based data centres, plus personal computing and vehicles.
MediaTek shares rose about 10% on 1 September.
signals.assessment: The structure is the point and it is now a pattern: a convertible rather than equity, the same shape as the $2.0bn of preferred stock Nvidia took in Marvell on 31 March. A supplier is being financed into building what the buyer needs, which keeps the ecosystem closed and moves capital-intensity onto the balance sheet of the company that already sets the standard.

signals.headline: China's CXMT began small-batch production of high-bandwidth memory, which is the ground this case actually stands on
summary: ChangXin Memory Technologies is producing HBM3E in small quantities for the first time, with Alibaba's T-Head and Cambricon testing it against their processors and commercial integration targeted for 2027.
That is one generation behind Samsung, SK hynix and Micron, which are in mass production on HBM4, and reporting puts CXMT three to five years behind technically with low yields.
It follows the LPDDR6 mass-production report of 30 August, which was mobile memory rather than high-bandwidth.
signals.assessment: The substitution argument has moved from mobile memory onto high-bandwidth memory, which is where this case rests, and that is a real advance on last week's boundary. It is still small-batch output of a superseded generation being sampled rather than shipped, so the timing is what changed rather than the conclusion. The dated invalidation to watch is Chinese HBM at commercial volume ahead of the 2028-2030 base case.

signals.headline: Samsung has committed about 70% of its memory output to contracts running to 2031, at roughly a fifth of the spot price
signals.src: Seoul Economic Daily / Wccftech / 24-7 Wall St. / SamMobile
summary: Samsung has placed roughly 70% of its memory production capacity under long-term agreements running to 2031, with Microsoft, Nvidia and Google named as counterparties (Seoul Economic Daily, 31 August).

The price gap inside those agreements is the striking part: a 36GB HBM3E module fetches about 2.87m Korean won on the spot market against 500,000-700,000 won under contract, roughly four to five times.
Buyers accepting five-year commitments at a discount are pricing scarcity that lasts, not scarcity that breaks.
signals.assessment: This is the clearest supply-side fact the memory case has carried, and it cuts both ways. Contracted volume at a fifth of spot removes the sequential price rollover that would invalidate the theme, because the earnings are no longer set by the open market; it also caps how much of a spot squeeze reaches the sellers. Trade press rather than a company filing, and carried as reported.

signals.headline: Delaware became the first state to make data centres build and pay for their own clean power
signals.src: State of Delaware / Sierra Club / DataCenterDynamics
summary: Governor Matt Meyer signed energy consumer protection legislation on 28 August 2026 requiring hyperscale data centres to generate their own clean energy over a ten-year period, matched to the state's renewable portfolio standard
A portion of their backup power must also come from clean sources, and the operators must pay for their own grid infrastructure costs under a binding agreement with the utility
The law removes the obligation to supply electricity to a large load where doing so would harm other customers - the first such provision in the United States
A companion measure strips data centres out of a state tax-incentive programme they previously qualified for
signals.assessment: This is the fourth authority in three weeks to reach the same conclusion, and the first to write it into statute rather than into a tariff or a filing. Georgia's regulator cleared a 3.2-gigawatt contract on the same principle, the largest US grid operator has asked federal regulators for the power to curtail loads that do not bring their own capacity, and Spain has drafted an hourly renewable-sourcing rule. Independent bodies converging on one answer is what a durable rule looks like. It also explains why the biggest projects are being built behind the meter: a campus that never connects is unaffected by any of it, and still orders the turbines.

signals.headline: Siemens Energy is selling the half of itself that AI does not need, and five buyout firms are bidding
summary: Siemens Energy has mandated Goldman Sachs to sell a majority stake in its Transformation of Industry division - steam turbines, compressors and hydrogen electrolysers - reported on 24 August
The division carries about EUR 5.7bn of revenue and 17,000 employees, and could be valued above EUR 10bn
CVC Capital Partners, EQT, Bain Capital, Brookfield and KKR are all weighing bids; the unit would be deconsolidated with the parent retaining a minority
The group's order backlog stands at about EUR 162bn after a record EUR 17.9bn of third-quarter intake reported on 5 August
signals.assessment: The European turbine incumbent is separating the part of its portfolio that serves the old industrial economy from the part that serves data centres, and private equity is willing to pay above EUR 10bn for the former. That is a flows signal about where the durable margin is thought to sit, expressed by five firms with no reason to agree with each other. The parent keeps the gas and grid businesses, which is the exposure this case is about.

signals.headline: Germany's listed submarine builder crossed EUR 25bn of orders, which answers the objection that there was nothing to own
summary: TKMS reported a EUR 20.1bn order backlog at its reporting date; a mid-August German Navy award for four MEKO A-200 frigates added about EUR 6.3bn, the largest surface-ship contract in the company's history, taking the total past EUR 25bn
Canada selected TKMS in July for up to twelve boats under its Patrol Submarine Project, with contract negotiations still under way
The company was spun out of thyssenkrupp and has traded in the Prime Standard segment of the Frankfurt exchange since 20 October 2025; thyssenkrupp retains 51%
Separately, Austal's board granted Hanwha four weeks of exclusive due diligence on 11 August over a US$1.05bn to US$1.2bn approach for its American yard
signals.assessment: Until now the industrial-policy case for shipbuilding pointed at two Korean yards, an American diversified prime with a shipyard inside it, and a privately held Quebec yard that has just won C$11.3bn of icebreaker work - none of which a European reader can hold as a pure exposure. A Frankfurt-listed builder with a decade of visible revenue is a different proposition. The qualification is the free float: thyssenkrupp still owns half the company, and no fund flows or sell-side coverage have moved toward the group, which is why this stays a watch rather than a conclusion.

signals.headline: TSMC has told its largest customers that wafer prices rise across every node in 2027
summary: Base wafer prices rise roughly 5% to 10% from the start of 2027 across all advanced nodes from 2-nanometre through 7, according to supply-chain reporting
Mature 12, 16 and 28-nanometre processes rise by up to 10% - the first mature-node increase in more than three years
Orders beyond a customer's original projection carry a further 10% to 15% surcharge, aimed at high-performance computing volumes
Nvidia, Apple, AMD and Qualcomm are among the customers told; TSMC took 73% of a foundry market that grew about 30% in the second quarter
signals.assessment: This is reported through the supply chain rather than announced, so it is carried as reported. If it holds it is a monopoly pricing its own queue rather than passing through a cost, and the mature-node increase is the tell: those lines have no AI scarcity behind them, so raising them is a statement about pricing power rather than about demand. The cost lands on the designers, which is a margin question for them and a revenue question for the foundry - and it is a reason to prefer the constrained supplier over the customer paying for the constraint.

signals.headline: Britain's regulator cleared private credit into workplace pensions, in the month private credit funds were still gated
signals.src: FCA Register / Professional Pensions / Investment Week
summary: The Financial Conduct Authority authorised a Legal & General and WTW private credit long-term asset fund on Wednesday 26 August, per the FCA's own register - three days earlier than the trade report that first carried it
It is L&G's first private markets vehicle of this kind and can invest across public and private markets including infrastructure, real estate and private credit
The regulator judged the vehicle suitable for defined-contribution pension schemes, which is the route by which ordinary British savers reach the asset class
Goldman Sachs is separately preparing a private equity fund for retail investors
signals.assessment: The rail is opening faster than the liquidity behind it is improving. Three large managers have gated retail private credit vehicles inside six months - Apollo capped withdrawals at 5% of shares in June after exit requests reached 16.8%, following Blackstone and Partners Group, and a Sydney-listed manager capped monthly redemptions at 1% of assets from 25 August. A defined-contribution saver reaching these assets through the newest wrapper meets that constraint last rather than first, which is the part worth knowing before the marketing arrives.

signals.headline: A Korean cell maker took a $1.09bn grid-storage order, the largest this cluster has recorded
signals.src: Korea Herald / The Elec / Seoul Economic Daily
summary: SK On agreed to supply 9 gigawatt-hours of lithium iron phosphate pouch cells to NeoVolta Power of the United States, roughly KRW 1.5tn or about $1.09bn
Cells come from SK On's Georgia plant across 2027 to 2031; NeoVolta assembles them into packs and supplies them back
The two companies plan to extend the partnership to a total of 18 gigawatt-hours, with a separate agreement targeted this year
SK Innovation shares rose about 6% on the announcement on 31 August
signals.assessment: The biggest and best-pinned number this cluster has produced, and it still resolves to a division of a Korean conglomerate rather than to anything a reader can own as pure exposure - which is the structural reason grid storage sits on the watch list rather than on the main one. What it does confirm is that American utility-scale procurement is being contracted years ahead and in lithium iron phosphate, not in the long-duration chemistries that generate most of the sector's headlines.

signals.headline: Brent settled $89.31 on Friday, a 0.43% fall rather than the 1.78% first recorded, and reopened above $90
summary: Brent settled $89.31 on Friday 28 August, down 0.43% on the day from $89.70 and 5.38% on the week from $94.39 on 21 August
The level first published for that session, $88.10, was a provisional point the source has since finalised
The contract reopened at $90.56 on the morning of 31 August, up 1.40%
Over the same week benchmark Gulf-to-China tanker earnings set a record $647,000 a day and European gas stores entered the heating season 63% full, the lowest in thirteen years
signals.assessment: The corrected number does not change the shape of the week - crude still fell and freight still set a record - but it removes a fourfold overstatement of Friday's move and restores a market that is drifting rather than breaking. That matters for how the whole premium is read: the barrels keep declining to price a disrupted strait, and every piece of evidence that the disruption is real now arrives through gas and freight instead.

signals.headline: A 2.67-gigawatt gas plant is being built for a Microsoft AI campus with no grid connection at all
summary: Chevron and Microsoft signed a 20-year power purchase agreement on 22 June 2026 for a co-located gas plant at a Microsoft AI campus near Pecos, Reeves County, West Texas
Known as Project Kilby: about 2.67 gigawatts at full build-out, with a stated long-term target of 5 gigawatts into the 2030s, on a site of more than 2,000 acres
It runs entirely behind the meter - no utility involvement and no ERCOT interconnection - with fuel taken directly from Chevron's own Permian production
GE Vernova turbines supply the bulk of the generation, with additional units from Caterpillar's Solar Turbines; power is expected from late 2028 and a final investment decision is due this year
signals.assessment: Every regulatory fight over large loads assumes the load wants to join the grid. This one does not. A campus that generates its own power, from its own gas, on its own land, needs no interconnection queue, no capacity charge and no state approval of a special tariff - and it still buys turbines. The equipment demand survives the siting argument entirely, which is why it is the more durable half of this case than the rulemaking is.

signals.headline: Samsung showed a drop-in memory part that triples AI inference throughput without changing the package
summary: Presented at Hot Chips 2026 on 25 August: LPDDR5X-PIM puts sixteen processing blocks, each a multiply-accumulate tree with an integer and floating-point unit, inside the memory arrays
Samsung measured 3.01 times the AI token throughput of standard LPDDR5X, with 614 GB/s of internal bandwidth in the same 561-ball package
Running Meta's Llama 3.1, throughput went from 27 to 81.3 tokens a second and task completion fell from 12.3 seconds to 5.4
This is a conference presentation rather than a product launch, and no availability date was given
signals.assessment: The memory shortage is priced on the assumption that high-bandwidth memory is the only way past the memory wall. A conventional low-power part that triples inference throughput in an unchanged package attacks the same problem from underneath, at a fraction of the cost and without the packaging bottleneck. It is a demonstration, not a shipment, and it is the most credible substitution risk this case has yet seen.

signals.headline: Supertanker earnings on the Gulf-to-China route hit a record $647,000 a day, more than ten times a year ago
summary: Ships carrying crude from Saudi Arabia to China earned a record $647,000 a day on Thursday 27 August, on Baltic Exchange assessments
Transits through the Strait of Hormuz have fallen from about 125 ships a day before the conflict escalated on 28 February 2026 to roughly 25
A separate assessment puts fixtures actually transiting Hormuz nearer $470,000 a day - a different route, not a contradiction
TotalEnergies' chief executive said moving a single cargo through Hormuz now costs about $20m
signals.assessment: Crude itself keeps falling - Brent settled $89.31 on Friday, down 5.4% on the week - while the cost of moving it sets records. That is the shape of a chokepoint rather than a shortage: the barrels exist, the freight to reach them does not. Tonnage is now the cleanest price expression of the blockade, and the only leg of this theme currently making new highs.

signals.headline: Canada awarded C$11.3bn for six polar icebreakers, the largest shipbuilding contract in Quebec's history
summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney announced the award to Chantier Davie at Levis, Quebec on 24 August 2026: six Polar Class 3 Canadian Coast Guard icebreakers
C$11.3bn, about US$8.2bn - the two figures reported in the same week are the same contract in different currencies
Steel cutting on the first vessel is scheduled for 2027, delivery in 2032, with the full fleet operational by 2038
The programme is expected to support close to 5,000 jobs and contribute about C$650m a year to Canadian output
signals.assessment: The largest Western naval order of the year has gone, for the second time, to a builder with no listed shares. That is the pattern that keeps this off the investible list rather than a reason to promote it: the policy is real, the contracts are real, and the equity route is not there. Until a listed Western yard wins work on this scale, the accessible expression remains the equipment suppliers, which is a different theme.

signals.headline: Taiwan's legislature passed a NT$240bn drone act and rejected the president's own special budget for it
signals.src: Hong Kong Free Press / Taipei Times / Manila Times
summary: On 27 August the Legislative Yuan passed, 60-50, an act authorising up to NT$240bn (about US$7.56bn) of drone spending over six years
It rejected the Cabinet's competing NT$210bn (about US$6.6bn) special budget bill, which would have been overseen by the defence ministry and run to the end of 2031
The version that passed funds roughly NT$40bn a year through the ordinary annual budget, with increases permitted
The two figures circulating this week are two different bills, and the larger one is the one that passed
signals.assessment: An annual appropriation is a weaker commitment than a ring-fenced special budget, because each year is a fresh vote. The headline number went up and the certainty behind it went down. For suppliers this is order flow with an election risk attached rather than a funded programme.

signals.headline: A London-listed flow-battery maker won the engineering contract for a 2.1 gigawatt-hour system in Switzerland
summary: Invinity Energy Systems confirmed the engineering, procurement and construction award on 24 August for what the trade press describes as a landmark 2.1GWh vanadium flow battery in Switzerland
Separately, Certain Energy, an Imperial College spin-out, raised GBP 10m in a Series A for manganese flow batteries and is planning an Indian grid project
Both are long-duration chemistries rather than lithium, aimed at the multi-hour firming that lithium serves expensively
signals.assessment: The long-duration case has been held back by a basket problem: the good news kept landing at conglomerates whose storage revenue is a line item, and only one constituent had a pinned price. Two European names with their own contracts and their own funding rounds is not a basket either, but it is the first time the long-duration leg has produced companies a European reader can actually identify.

signals.headline: India's regulator cleared what would be its largest ever listing, days after Shein cut its own target to $27bn
summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India cleared Jio Platforms' draft prospectus on 28 August for an offering reported around $4bn - which would be India's largest listing
Seven approvals went through together, and India's disclosed pipeline is now about Rs 4.72 lakh crore
Shein is targeting about $27bn in a Hong Kong listing, a fraction of the roughly $100bn it was valued at in 2022, after a London listing did not proceed
Westinghouse has filed confidentially in the United States and Ursa Major agreed a $2.3bn merger with a listed shell
signals.assessment: The window is open in volume and closed on price. Issuers are getting away, and they are getting away at valuations set years lower than the private marks they carried in. That combination clears the backlog without re-rating the asset class, which is a healthier reopening than the alternative and a worse one for anyone holding the old marks.

signals.headline: Four first-of-their-kind device authorisations cleared American regulators inside a single week
summary: Abbott received authorisation on 25 August for the first wearable that measures glucose and ketones at the same time, with a US launch planned this year
Roche was cleared for the Elecsys pTau217 blood test, used to rule Alzheimer's pathology in or out; Quest will offer it
The first fully autonomous robotic blood-draw device was authorised, into a shortage of phlebotomists
Avulux received a De Novo authorisation that creates the first device classification for migraine light sensitivity, and Johnson & Johnson's OTTAVA surgical robot was approved
signals.assessment: Six consecutive cycles here were recorded as quiet, on the reasonable ground that a device approval at a mega-cap is not a theme. Four firsts in one week is a different observation: the regulator is clearing categories, not just products. It still does not make a basket - the beneficiaries are Abbott, Roche, Johnson & Johnson and Philips, for whom this is a small part of the business - and that is now the stated reason this stays off the list rather than an absence of evidence.

signals.headline: Rocket Lab sold a full flight of a rocket that has never flown, and its hypersonic backlog reached about $500m
signals.src: The Motley Fool / SpaceNews / Space Connect
summary: Kepler Communications bought a dedicated Neutron launch, reported on 29 August - the first full-vehicle commercial sale for a rocket still awaiting its debut
The company also won a $12m US Space Force data-network contract in the same week

The suborbital hypersonic programme adds to about $500m in total: $266m from the Space Force for twelve flights, $190m from the Navy for twenty, $30m from Anduril for three, and $15-20m of individual missions
That is a cumulative backlog across four customers, not a single award, and it is more than half of the company's projected 2026 revenue of $953m
signals.assessment: The market is pricing this name on one unflown rocket while a suborbital defence business quietly became half the revenue base. The Neutron sale matters for the same reason: a customer paying for a full flight before a first launch is a harder commitment than a manifest slot. The debut date is still the risk, and the company has not re-dated it despite coverage saying it has slipped.

signals.headline: Europe got its first named humanoids-as-a-service company, and it raised EUR 1.7m
summary: Motion, based in Brussels, raised EUR 1.7m (about $2m) in pre-seed funding on 27 August to deploy humanoid robots into European factories on a rental model
Bosch has committed to an August 2027 humanoid production line at Buhl in Germany, working with the British maker Humanoid and with Schaeffler as an early customer
BMW is testing Figure's third-generation robot for logistics sequencing at Spartanburg
Against that, Reuters reported on 27 August from Chinese factories that the machines cannot yet do useful production work
signals.assessment: The rental model now has a European company attached to it, and that company is a pre-seed raise of under two million euros. That is the whole argument for watching this rather than owning it: the criteria for funding, policy and distinctness are all met, and the entire European service layer is smaller than a rounding error in the theme it belongs to.

signals.headline: The Fed chair told Jackson Hole inflation is too high, and a September rate rise went from a third to a coin flip
summary: Kevin Warsh, 28 August: the Fed's predominant focus right now should be on prices, and inflation is not meaningfully slowing
He also said the labour market is effectively at full employment and financial conditions may not be restraining the economy much
CME fed funds futures moved the September rate-rise probability to roughly 56-59%, from about 35% the day before
Kalshi put the odds of a quarter-point increase at 48%; Polymarket's odds of a 2026 increase rose to about 69% from the mid-50s
Short-dated Treasury yields jumped more than long-dated ones; the 30-year sits near a 19-year high
signals.assessment: This is the first time this year that a rate rise, rather than a pause, has been the market's central case for the next meeting. It reprices every long-duration asset on the page and it is why gold fell on a day when nothing changed about central-bank demand.

signals.headline: A federal appeals court ruled that states may treat sports prediction contracts as gambling, and split the circuits doing it
summary: Ninth Circuit, 28 August, unanimous: Kalshi's sports event contracts likely fail the Commodity Exchange Act definition of a swap
Federal commodities law therefore likely does not pre-empt Nevada from applying its gambling rules
The decision conflicts with a Third Circuit ruling in Kalshi's favour, which is the classic trigger for Supreme Court review
Around twenty states are litigating the same question; Kentucky sued the same week and a British Columbia regulator reached the same conclusion
signals.assessment: The question of who regulates event contracts was open on Thursday and had an answer on Friday, and the answer went against a single federal regime. Anyone sizing this market as a nationally licensed asset class now has to price fifty jurisdictions and a probable Supreme Court term.

signals.headline: Washington guaranteed floor prices for two heavy rare earths for the first time, inside a $1.55bn Brazilian structure
signals.src: Metal Tech News / Baltimore Sun / Epoch Times
summary: The Department of War announced on 24 August that a special-purpose vehicle it backs has completed a $1.55bn capitalisation
Its own commitment was upsized from $500m to $750m, into US SIIE LLC through the Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment programme
Guaranteed minimum prices: terbium $2,050/kg, dysprosium $575/kg, neodymium-praseodymium $110/kg, each rising 2% a year
The offtake supports Serra Verde's Pela Ema mine and processing project in Brazil
signals.assessment: A floor price turns a commodity into a contracted revenue line, and this is the second time the mechanism has been used after the neodymium floor set with MP Materials. Applying it to dysprosium and terbium reaches the two elements that make magnets survive jet-engine and missile temperatures, which is where the Chinese chokehold actually binds.

signals.headline: The US Army committed up to $2.2bn to put more than twenty commercial microreactors on five bases
signals.src: US Army / Breaking Defense / POWER Magazine
summary: Announced 26 August under the Janus programme: up to $2.2bn across five years for more than twenty reactors
Five vendors named - Antares Nuclear at Fort Bragg, BWXT Advanced Technologies at Fort Campbell, General Atomics at Fort Hood, Radiant at Fort Benning, Westinghouse Government Services at Fort Drum
BWXT's unit is a 20MWe design scaled up from the 1.5MWe Project Pele reactor it has been building since 2020
Separately, Oklo agreed a 1.2GW supply arrangement with Meta for Ohio data centres by 2030, and Centrus signed to deliver it enriched fuel from 2029
signals.assessment: Small reactors have had roadmaps and executive orders for two years and very few orders. This is a customer with appropriated money naming sites and dates, and it is the strongest single week the sector has had. Only one of the five vendors is directly listed, which is the whole difficulty with the sector.

signals.headline: The Chinese memory maker named in the own invalidation reported revenue up 874% and profit of RMB 77.6bn
signals.src: South China Morning Post / Barron’s / MarketWatch
summary: CXMT first-half 2026 revenue RMB 150.31bn (about $22.4bn), up 873.6% year on year against pre-listing guidance of RMB 110-120bn
Net profit attributable to shareholders RMB 77.61bn, against a RMB 2.33bn loss a year earlier and guidance of RMB 50-57bn
DDR-series revenue RMB 69.47bn, 46.3% of main business revenue, up from 31.9% in 2025
These are its first results since a Shanghai listing that made it China's most valuable listed company
signals.assessment: The shortage case rests on supply not arriving. Supply is arriving, at scale, from outside the three incumbents - but in conventional DDR5 rather than high-bandwidth memory, so the stated invalidation, which is written around high-bandwidth memory, still has not triggered. The invalidation is the thing that needs rewriting, not the case.

signals.headline: A French quantum hardware maker listed on Nasdaq and nearly doubled, and Ottawa lent Xanadu C$195m to build a factory
signals.src: Pasqal / The Quantum Insider / Government of Canada
summary: Pasqal Holding began trading as PSQL on 28 August with about $360m of cash and a valuation near $2bn; the shares closed the first day at $19.11, up 95.2%
Canada committed C$195m through the Strategic Response Fund as a revenue-linked loan to Xanadu, which has been public since March
It anchors a C$893m project to build Inception, a 158,000 sq ft photonics manufacturing site in Toronto - the largest government quantum-manufacturing commitment in Canadian history
IBM completed its acquisition of HRL Laboratories; EuroHPC selected thirteen European quantum-processor startups
signals.assessment: Money stopped being the constraint here weeks ago; what was missing was the market paying for it. A debut that doubles is one listing rather than a cohort re-rating, so the price leg is still the failing one - but a European pure play is now buyable in dollars, which it was not a week ago.

signals.headline: An ASX-listed manager capped monthly withdrawals from its private credit funds at 1% of assets
summary: MA Financial Group, effective 25 August, limited each monthly redemption period on the MA Secured Loan Series to up to 1% of funds under management
The cap flows through to feeder funds that invest in the series, including the listed MA Credit Income Trust
The manager runs about A$2.1bn in the affected strategies and has played down the impact
In the same week the Financial Times reported a broader redemption wave in private credit funds sold to wealthy individuals
signals.assessment: This is the exact mismatch the assessment was opened to watch: monthly liquidity promised on loans that do not repay monthly. It has now happened at a named, listed manager rather than in the abstract, which makes the risk checkable - and it argues for listed trusts at a discount over evergreen funds at par.

signals.headline: Europe enters winter with gas stores 63% full, the lowest going into a heating season since 2013
summary: EU stocks were 63% full in the final week of August against an average near 80% for the date
At the current injection rate the bloc enters the heating season about a fifth below the five-year average
QatarEnergy extended its force majeure into October; Qatari exports are down 96% with the Strait of Hormuz disrupted for six months
Goldman Sachs estimates December TTF would need to exceed EUR 100/MWh, against its own EUR 50 base case, to refill storage if exports normalise only gradually
signals.assessment: The gas leg of the assessment now has a quantity, a date and a supplier who has said in writing that he will not deliver. That is a firmer footing than the crude leg, where Brent settled $89.70 and is down 4.35% on the week - the premium has migrated from oil to gas and the entry should be read that way.

signals.headline: Canada set counter-tariffs of 15% to 50% on C$27.6bn of US goods, effective 8 September
summary: Announced 25 August after talks collapsed: C$27.6bn (about US$19.94bn), matching Washington dollar for dollar across roughly 700 products
50% on steel, aluminium, furniture and clothing; 25% on cheese, appliances and some seafood; 15% on electronics and tools
Trump's 50% duties on about $20bn of Canadian imports took effect the same week
Ottawa added a C$7.5bn support package for affected workers and businesses
signals.assessment: The aluminium question is now settled by both governments' own actions: the talks failed and the 50% duty stands, against a market that buys most of its aluminium from Canada and has no near-term substitute. 8 September is a dated event, not a threat.

signals.headline: The annual benchmark revision cut US employment by 79,000, where economists had expected an increase of 183,000
signals.src: Bureau of Labor Statistics / Bloomberg / Yahoo Finance
summary: Preliminary benchmark released 28 August: total non-farm employment through March 2026 overstated by 79,000, or 0.1%
Total private employment revised down 178,000, also 0.1%
Economists surveyed by Bloomberg had expected an upward revision of 183,000
The final revision arrives with the January 2027 employment report in February 2027
signals.assessment: A tenth of a percent is a rounding error next to the 818,000 cut for March 2024, so the case that the labour market is quietly far weaker than the monthly prints lost its main statistical support. That is why the Fed chair could call the labour market effectively at full employment on the same day.

signals.headline: TSMC took 73% of a foundry market that grew 29% in a quarter, and Washington moved to close the remote-access route to Chinese buyers
signals.src: Counterpoint via Yonhap / The Information / Tom’s Hardware
summary: Second-quarter global foundry revenue rose about 29%, with TSMC at 73% share and Samsung at 7%
The administration is preparing a rule to curb Chinese access to advanced chips rented remotely from offshore servers, possibly shared with industry in September
The US is probing Singapore-based Apex Logistics over suspected Nvidia chip shipments to China
Intel raised $23bn to fund AI chip capacity; AWS added a further two million Nvidia GPUs after its first million ran out early
signals.assessment: Remote access has been the standing gap in export control since the first diffusion rule: you cannot ship the chip, so you rent time on it. Closing it would be the first control that reaches compute rather than hardware, and the foundry share numbers say who has the capacity that would be rationed.

signals.headline: The rating agency's $1.3tn figure is now on its own masthead, and the chip designer is lending into its own demand
signals.src: S&P Global Ratings / Stock Titan / PIMCO via Startup Fortune
summary: S&P Global Ratings published its own note on 27 August: AI infrastructure investment to exceed $1.3tn by 2027
Nvidia invested $2bn in Marvell, adding to a pattern of the largest supplier funding its own customers and suppliers
PIMCO warned that AI-related debt issuance is growing faster than bond markets can absorb it
Nvidia's finance chief said about half of data-centre revenue now comes from customers other than the hyperscalers
signals.assessment: Demand for this build has been settled for a quarter; the open question is who carries the balance sheet. A supplier taking equity in its buyers, GPU-collateralised lending and a bond manager warning on issuance speed are three different descriptions of the same financing strain.

signals.headline: A German state, a listed utility and the Max Planck Institute signed up to build a stellarator power plant
summary: Proxima Fusion signed a memorandum of understanding with Bavaria, RWE and Max Planck's Institute for Plasma Physics on 28 August
The Department of Energy approved Xcimer Energy's laser fusion power plant design the same week
Both follow the Reuters-reported US roadmap targeting fusion deployment by the mid-2030s
Commonwealth Fusion's widely reshared '$4bn' is cumulative capital raised, following a $1bn round announced on 30 July, not a new raise
signals.assessment: A listed European utility putting its name to a plant is the first counterparty here a reader could actually own. It is a memorandum rather than a contract, and every developer in the field remains private, so the access problem is unchanged.

signals.headline: Chinese storage installations fell 18% in the first half while its exporters' order books rose 83%
signals.src: ESS News / Battery Technology / Wood Mackenzie
summary: China's new-type energy storage additions fell 18% year on year in the first half of 2026; overseas orders rose 83%
Cummins won its largest battery storage contract to date, for a US data centre
GE Vernova took the third-stage contract at Queensland's 780MW / 3,075MWh Supernode project
Wood Mackenzie raised its Latin American storage forecast to 34GW by 2035
signals.assessment: Demand did not fall, it moved: a subsidy-driven home market cooling while export order books nearly double is the shape of an industry becoming a global supplier. The data-centre contracts are the more investible half, because they attach storage to the one demand curve nobody disputes.

signals.headline: Reuters reported that China's humanoids can win medals and still cannot do factory work
summary: Two Reuters pieces on 27 August concluded that Chinese humanoid robots are not yet capable enough to replace factory labour
XPeng's robotics arm raised $900m at a $6.3bn valuation; Bosch is working with a European humanoid maker toward commercialisation
Nevada approved paid driverless deployments and Las Vegas cleared up to 8,000 robotaxis
The London robotaxi rollout slipped again for want of Transport for London guidance
signals.assessment: Humanoid robotics-as-a-service meets all five of its criteria on funding, product and policy, and reporters who visited the factories say the machines do not yet do the job they are sold for. That is why it stays pre-investible on a full score.

signals.headline: Washington put $300m behind faster optical links between AI chips
signals.src: Reuters via AOL / TechInsights / company results
summary: The US is to award GlobalFoundries about $300m to develop faster interconnects for AI chips
Powertech's fan-out panel-level packaging capacity is fully booked by AMD and Broadcom, with co-packaged optics targeted for mass production in mid-2027
Zhongji Innolight's first-half net profit rose about 2.4 times; Yangtze Optical Fibre's rose nearly nine times
Quintessent raised a $40m Series A for quantum-dot lasers aimed at cutting data-movement power by 40%
signals.assessment: Government money entering the interconnect layer is new; until now the public dollars went to fabs and the optics were left to the market. Chinese module makers reporting profits up multiples in the same week says the bottleneck is being paid for at both ends of the supply chain.

signals.headline: Gold settled $4,478.10 on the Jackson Hole speech, a 2.85% fall rather than the 1.73% first recorded
signals.src: Yahoo Finance chart series (GC=F) / Business Times / IndexBox
summary: Gold settled $4,478.10 on Friday 28 August, down 2.85% on the day and 3.16% on the week from $4,624.10 on 21 August
It traded above $4,600 that morning and below $4,500 after the Fed chair's Jackson Hole keynote moved the odds of a September rate rise from about a third to roughly a coin flip

The level first published for that session, $4,529.90, was a provisional point the source has since finalised; same-day and weekend coverage both described the fall as about 3%, which matches the settled figure
At $4,478.10 the metal is almost exactly 20% below its $5,597.23 peak of 29 January 2026; it traded $4,485 on the morning of 31 August
signals.assessment: The direction was never in doubt and the size was. A 2.85% session is the first genuine defeat the rate path has handed this metal since July, and it is two-thirds larger than the number first carried. The official bid underneath - a record 289 tonnes of central-bank buying in the second quarter - is a structural fact and a speech does not touch it. What a speech does touch is the opportunity cost of holding an asset that pays nothing, and that is now being repriced upward by three forecasting houses at once.

signals.headline: The US bank regulator proposed stablecoin rules and four of the largest banks began discussing a joint issuer
summary: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency proposed rules governing stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act on 27 August, after the statutory rulemaking deadline was missed
JPMorgan, Bank of America, Wells Fargo and Santander are exploring a global stablecoin consortium
The Bank of England was given a stablecoin innovation objective; the ECB's Isabel Schnabel argued for central-bank money to move on-chain
Bitcoin fell 3.2% to $77,693 on 29 August as rate-rise odds rose
signals.assessment: The regulatory leg has been the strong one for months and it just got stronger on both sides of the Atlantic. The change worth marking is the incumbent banks moving from lobbying against the rules to organising an issuer under them.

signals.headline: Canada awarded C$8.2bn for six coast guard icebreakers, to a yard nobody can buy
summary: Davie was awarded an $8.2bn contract for six Canadian Coast Guard icebreakers on 26 August
Cosco booked another multi-billion-yuan containership order; Veritas placed two 64,000 dwt bulkers at Cosco's Zhoushan yard
Saronic topped out a $300m Louisiana shipyard expansion; CORE POWER is targeting first US nuclear-powered ship construction from 2028
Thyssenkrupp's marine business is expanding capacity against submarine tenders from Ottawa to New Delhi
signals.assessment: The order book for Western naval and icebreaker tonnage is real and growing, and the yards taking it are private or state-owned. That gap between a visible demand curve and an unbuyable supply side is exactly why this stays on the radar rather than in the book.

signals.headline: A US tungsten scrap export ban took effect and domestic miners rose about 70% in a month
summary: The US ban on tungsten scrap exports came into force, with domestic tungsten miners up around 70% over the month
Reuters commentary on 27 August: the US needs more aluminium and needs it now, with new smelters years away
Nickel eased as rate-rise fears offset dollar weakness and a persistent supply surplus
Iran said the Strait of Hormuz would not reopen immediately, keeping the freight and energy premium in metals pricing
signals.assessment: Restricting scrap exports is the cheapest industrial policy available: it needs no appropriation and it works on a timescale of weeks rather than the decade a smelter takes. Expect the instrument to be reused, which makes the scrap-linked names the ones to watch rather than the miners.

signals.headline: A Thames Water drought pilot raised forever-chemical levels, days before the US comment window closes
summary: The Guardian reported on 27 August that PFAS concentrations surged during a pilot of a Thames Water plan to combat drought
The EPA's replacement of its withdrawn biosolids risk assessment with voluntary guidance is open for comment until 4 September
France faces an estimated EUR 5.7bn bill to deal with forever chemicals
A Congressional Research Service paper catalogued July's water-system cyber incidents
signals.assessment: The two sides of the assessment moved further apart: European liability keeps hardening while US federal rulemaking softens into guidance. A British utility creating a contamination problem while solving a supply one is the clearest illustration yet that the compliance spend is not optional.

signals.headline: The US has burned through key missile stocks and says rebuilding will take five years
summary: Military.com reported on 27 August that rebuilding depleted US missile stockpiles may take five years
A $533m US artillery plant has produced no shells, according to reporting the same week
Wolfram Europa plans a EUR 200m explosives complex in Latvia for RDX, HMX, warheads and anti-tank mines
Italy formally requested EUR 8bn under SAFE after Romania received its first EUR 2.5bn payment
signals.assessment: Order books are records and have been for a year; the constraint has moved to whether anyone can build the things. That is a late-stage pattern - the opportunity has been recognised and paid for, and the remaining upside sits with whoever solves delivery rather than whoever wins the order.

signals.headline: Nvidia closed 9.1% higher, its biggest session since April 2025, and carried an index whose members mostly fell
summary: Nvidia fell about 4% on the initial print, reversed, opened roughly 6% higher and closed +9.1%
About $442bn of market value added - the largest single-day gain since April 2025
S&P 500 +0.72% to 7,730.99 and Nasdaq Composite about +1.4%, with Salesforce +22% and Okta +28%
Most S&P 500 constituents finished lower on the day
signals.assessment: A record-sized single-stock move carrying a broad index whose members mostly fell is a narrowing of leadership, not a broadening of it, and it is the reason the breadth reading deteriorated on a strong day.

signals.headline: A rating agency put the AI build's cash burn at three straight years for all six of the largest spenders
summary: Combined hyperscaler capital spending expected to exceed $1.3 trillion by 2027
Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle and SpaceX all expected to generate negative free operating cash flow in 2026 and 2027
Recovery in free cash flow not projected until 2029
Debt, leases, guarantees, joint ventures, special-purpose vehicles and residual-value guarantees named as increasingly important funding routes
signals.assessment: The demand side of this build was answered in Nvidia's 26 August filing; the financing side is answered here, and the answer is that the payers spend more than they earn for three consecutive years. Both are true at once.

signals.headline: Georgia's regulator cleared a 3.2 gigawatt supply contract in which the data centre pays for its own generation
signals.src: Georgia PSC via DatacenterDynamics / CBS / RTO Insider
summary: Georgia Power will develop 3.2GW of new generation for an OpenAI data centre in Effingham County (Project Camellia)
OpenAI commits to pay the full cost of the infrastructure required to serve it
Up to 1GW of flexible demand response offered; delivery between 2028 and 2032
Stated $20bn investment; commission staff reviewed and declined to object rather than holding a public vote
signals.assessment: The question of who pays for data-centre power was settled here in favour of the customer paying, which is what turns a siting constraint into an equipment order rather than a rate increase.

signals.headline: The largest US grid operator asked federal regulators to let it curtail large loads that do not bring their own capacity
signals.src: PJM Inside Lines / White & Case / Virginia Mercury
summary: Filed with federal regulators on 13 August, following a 31 July filing that would pay up to $20bn for new plants serving data centres built through 2027
Creates an Interim Resource Adequacy Service charge for new large loads
Loads can reduce or eliminate the charge through Bring Your Own New Capacity - new generation, uprates, surplus interconnection, repowering, fuel conversion or storage
PJM has asked for an order effective no later than 12 October 2026
signals.assessment: The same principle Georgia applied to one contract, applied by rule across the largest grid in the country. Four jurisdictions have now written a version of it, and every version is demand for generation, switchgear and storage.

signals.headline: Three Federal Reserve officials argued in one day that policy is not restrictive enough
summary: Kansas City's Jeffrey Schmid: inflation 'still stubborn and still sticky'; policy 'might be accommodative on the short end'
