Cleveland's Beth Hammack: it will take more than one rate increase to bring inflation down
Boston's Susan Collins as counterweight: the July report does not change her view that policy is restrictive and disinflation will be gradual
Kevin Warsh gives his first Jackson Hole keynote as chair on 28 August
signals.assessment: A sitting regional president describing policy as possibly accommodative is a step beyond the three dissents for a rise at the July meeting, and it is the clearest hawkish escalation since that vote.

signals.headline: Weekly jobless claims fell to 203,000 and continuing claims to 1.778m
summary: Initial claims 203,000, below expectations
Continuing claims 1.778m, also below forecast
Insured unemployment rate held steady; July goods trade deficit widened
Coverage describes a 'no hire, no fire' market in which layoffs stay low and hiring does not resume
signals.assessment: This removes the labour-market argument for waiting without supplying evidence of overheating, and it is the third consecutive print in which the labour market has refused to turn.

signals.headline: Europe signed EUR 543.6m of launch contracts and none of the three winners is listed
signals.src: ESA via Euronews / European Spaceflight / Aviation Week
summary: Isar Aerospace EUR 197.8m for Spectrum; Rocket Factory Augsburg EUR 186.9m for RFA One, flying from SaxaVord in Shetland
PLD Space EUR 158.9m for Miura 5, financed mainly by Spain with German support
Talks continue with ArianeGroup's MaiaSpace; roughly EUR 900m committed to the programme since the November 2025 Bremen ministerial
Stated aim is a European successor to Ariane 6 before 2030 that does not depend on a single operator
signals.assessment: The first sovereign European launch money of its kind, and it lands entirely on private companies - a European reader can watch the capability being funded and has no direct way to own it.

signals.headline: Goldman Sachs put EUR 100 on the December gas price Europe needs to refill storage
summary: December Dutch TTF would likely need to exceed EUR 100/MWh if Middle East exports normalise only gradually through 2027
That is about 110% above Goldman's own base case of EUR 50/MWh
European storage about 62% full, the lowest for the time of year in nearly two decades
Benchmark trading near EUR 67/MWh in late August; Asian spot LNG above $22, a three-year high
signals.assessment: The gas leg now has a scenario price rather than an adjective, and it is the leg moving against the consumer while the crude leg has stopped falling - the two are no longer usefully described as one trade.

signals.headline: Revolut launched a licensed euro stablecoin and dropped Tether across Europe on the same day
summary: EURR is an Ethereum-based euro token issued through Stripe's Bridge
Bridge mints it under a Markets in Crypto-Assets service-provider licence and a Luxembourg electronic-money authorisation
Live first in Denmark, Poland and Portugal, with wider European availability planned
Revolut serves more than 80 million customers and withdrew support for Tether across Europe at the same time
signals.assessment: A licensed issuer displacing an unlicensed one inside a working regime, in Europe, while the equivalent US rulemaking has missed its statutory deadline and banks lobby to slow it further.

signals.headline: The Chinese memory maker that would break the shortage case is shipping into a flagship phone
summary: CXMT shares are reported up about 580% since the 27 July Shanghai listing
Its LPDDR6 is reported to have been designed into a Xiaomi flagship
The company is reported to be moving to hafnium transistors toward a 1a node, targeting 800,000 wafers a month by 2031
Against it, Nvidia's own commentary points to the memory bottleneck lasting into 2028
signals.assessment: A funded competitor becoming a shipped part is the clearest challenge the memory case has faced, and it arrives in the same week as the strongest demand evidence it has held.

signals.headline: Waymo confirmed Munich for 2027 in the week the London rollout slipped
signals.src: Waymo blog via CNBC / electrive / The Local
summary: Announced in a Waymo blog post on 25 August; Munich targeted by the end of 2027
Would be the first regular driverless robotaxi service in the European Union
Validation-driver testing with Jaguar I-PACE vehicles begins in Munich within weeks to map the network
Waymo Germany GmbH was registered in Munich in mid-June
signals.assessment: Continental Europe has moved ahead of the United Kingdom on the one autonomy leg where a UK reader had the closer exposure, and the London delay is a regulatory-guidance problem rather than a technical one.

signals.headline: The National Science Foundation put $290m across eight quantum institutes aimed at manufacturing, not physics
summary: More than $290m across eight university-led Quantum Leap Challenge Institutes, announced 25 August
Three new institutes and five renewals; roughly $28-37m each over five years
Led by Harvard, Yale, Princeton, Berkeley, Chicago, Colorado, Illinois and Maryland
Explicitly targeted at reliability, scalability and manufacturing rather than fundamental science
signals.assessment: Public money is no longer this category's constraint. The listed pure plays still trade below the index they are supposed to be leading, and that price leg is the only one still failing.

signals.headline: Lynas posted a record year and the currency confusion around it resolves
signals.src: Lynas FY26 results via Kalkine / Motley Fool AU / Bloomberg
summary: FY2026 revenue A$977.9m against A$556.5m; net profit after tax A$222.4m against A$8.0m
Record average selling price of $80.7/kg of rare-earth oxide
Rare-earth oxide output +25% to 13,089 tonnes; neodymium-praseodymium +11% to 7,260 tonnes
Malaysian operating licence renewed for ten years from March 2026; the result missed profit forecasts on rising capital costs
signals.assessment: The widely quoted '$703m record revenue' is the US dollar translation of the Australian figure, not a separate number. The record is real and so is the cost overrun behind the profit miss.

signals.headline: The liability is settled law while the rulebook behind it is being pulled back
summary: The D.C. Circuit upheld the Superfund hazardous-substance designation for PFOA and PFOS on 18 August
The Environmental Protection Agency withdrew its own draft risk assessment of the same chemicals in sewage sludge in July
It was replaced on 1 July by voluntary draft guidance with a comment period closing 4 September 2026
France faces an estimated EUR 5.7bn bill to deal with its own contamination
signals.assessment: Litigation is hardening the liability while rulemaking softens the obligation, which is a genuinely two-sided regulatory picture rather than the one-way tightening this category has been described as.

signals.headline: The prediction-market fight is now a federal-versus-state preemption battle with about twenty states litigating
signals.src: New York Times via CNBC / PYMNTS
summary: Roughly 20 states are litigating whether event-contract exchanges must follow state sports-gambling rules
A 44-state coalition has branded them a 'new form of casino'
Kalshi received clearance for margin trading for professional clients on 27 August
Reporting on 27 August described remarks made in New Orleans in spring 2026 arguing for federal rather than state oversight; the speaker advises one exchange and sits on another's board
signals.assessment: The reporting is this week's; the remarks are not. The dated, live facts are the litigation count, the state coalition and the margin clearance - a category whose regulatory outcome is now a preemption question rather than a licensing one.

signals.headline: Nvidia's fiscal Q2 revenue doubled to $96.2bn and the guide assumes no China data-centre revenue at all
summary: Revenue $96.2bn, +18% q/q and +106% y/y; Data Center $89.0bn, +117% y/y
GAAP EPS $2.46, non-GAAP $2.22; GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin 75.0%
Q3 outlook $108.0bn +/-2% at a 74.0% margin, explicitly assuming no Data Center compute revenue from China
Jensen Huang: 'We have supply for 70% growth' for fiscal 2028; Colette Kress says the company remains supply constrained
signals.assessment: The largest outstanding test of AI-capex conversion resolves decisively in favour of the demand case, and the China exposure that dominated this category for two months is now upside rather than a dependency.

signals.headline: Nvidia's committed supply more than doubled to $279bn, primarily to procure memory
signals.src: NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 CFO commentary / CNBC
summary: Supply commitments rose from $119bn in the prior quarter to $279bn
The company states the increase relates primarily to the procurement of memory
Memory names rose overnight: Micron, SanDisk, Samsung and SK hynix all higher
TrendForce now sizes DRAM and NAND at roughly 68% of major cloud providers' 2027 capital spending
signals.assessment: A filed contractual obligation from the largest buyer in the chain, more than doubling in three months - the strongest single piece of evidence this case has produced, and enough to restore conviction to 5.

signals.headline: CrowdStrike posted record net new recurring revenue and raised its full-year outlook by 6.3 points
summary: Revenue $1.47bn (+26%); annual recurring revenue $5.84bn (+25%)
Net new ARR $332.8m, a company record and +51% year on year
Full-year net-new ARR growth outlook raised 630bp to 34% at the midpoint; year-end ARR guided to $6.603-6.612bn
Record quarterly operating cash flow of $530m; shares +10.4% after hours to $208.81
signals.assessment: The first clean evidence that this category's threat record is converting into budget. One vendor is not a sector - Palo Alto Networks on 1 September is the confirming test.

signals.headline: The US Army committed up to $2.2bn to put more than twenty microreactors on five bases
summary: Janus programme: five vendors, five bases, up to $2.2bn combined through fiscal 2031
BWX Technologies at Fort Campbell, Westinghouse Government Services at Fort Drum, General Atomics at Fort Hood, Radiant at Fort Benning, Antares at Fort Bragg
Radiant disclosed the largest single share: up to $750m for fifteen 1-MWe Kaleidos units by 2030
Separately, Centrus agreed high-assay low-enriched fuel supply with Oklo for 2029 delivery
signals.assessment: Appropriated money reaching reactor builders rather than the fuel cycle - the leg this case was missing. Conviction raised from 3 to 4.

signals.headline: Washington guaranteed floor prices for dysprosium and terbium for the first time
signals.src: US Department of War / USA Rare Earth (GlobeNewswire) / Metal Tech News
summary: $750m into US SIIE LLC via the Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment programme, inside a $1.55bn structure
Supports Serra Verde's Pela Ema project in Brazil; phase-one output ~4,000 t REO equivalent a year by end-2026
Contractual floors: $2,050/kg terbium, $575/kg dysprosium, $110/kg neodymium-praseodymium, each rising 2% a year
Niron Magnetics separately received a conditional $150m commitment from the same department
signals.assessment: The neodymium-praseodymium floor is set exactly where the ex-China spot price had been slipping through, which is the specific two-sided problem in this category: the curbs bind and the western price falls anyway.

signals.headline: Anthropic agreed to pay Nscale about $45bn over six years for 460MW of Vera Rubin capacity
summary: Roughly $45bn over six years for about 460MW at Nscale's West Virginia campus, online at the end of 2027
Capacity is Nvidia Vera Rubin; Microsoft held a letter of intent on the same site in March and withdrew during the summer
Nscale is British, privately held, and reported to be targeting a US listing as soon as September
Sourced to people familiar rather than to a company release
signals.assessment: The contracted multi-year offtake this case has been asking for - and both counterparties are private, so it reaches the listed cohort only as read-across. Conviction held at 3.

signals.headline: Lumentum rose 6% and Coherent added 3.4% after hours as the optics price leg turned
summary: Lumentum closed $939.03 on 26 Aug, +6.04%, 13.5% below its $1,085.68 52-week high
Coherent closed $294.37, 33.1% below its $440.00 high, and traded $304.23 after hours (+3.35%)
The US is awarding GlobalFoundries $300m to develop faster AI chip links
Powertech's fan-out panel-level capacity is fully booked by AMD and Broadcom, with co-packaged optics to follow
signals.assessment: The demand record was never the broken part of this case; the price leg was, and it turned on a dated session. Two cleanly dated closes replace the ambiguous quotes carried since 19 August.

signals.headline: Rocket Lab posted record revenue of $234m while the shares sat 56% below their high
summary: Q2 revenue a record $234m, +62% year on year, on a $2.36bn backlog
Shares closed $66.18 on 26 Aug, 56% below a 52-week high of $151.00
The company replaced the equity deal that was funding its Iridium acquisition
Neutron: a first-stage propellant tank ruptured in a hydrostatic pressure test on 21 January at the Maryland facility, attributed to a manufacturing fault
signals.assessment: The tank failure caused January's slip to the fourth quarter, not this week's narrowing of the launch window, which comes from the chief executive's Q2 remarks. Coverage has run two events several months apart together.

signals.headline: Qatari LNG exports have collapsed 96% with cargoes stranded for six months
summary: Qatari gas has been stranded for six months; US sales are rising and European stocks are falling
European storage remains at its lowest seasonal level in records beginning in 2009
September TTF is the most expensive since 2023, with coverage discussing a move above EUR 100/MWh this winter
The EU faces an estimated EUR 41bn of additional fossil-fuel costs
signals.assessment: Crude and European gas are no longer one trade. Brent has fallen 7.8% on the week to $86.43 while the gas leg tightens into winter; a single conviction number over both now understates one side and overstates the other.

signals.headline: Central banks bought a record 289 tonnes in the second quarter as gold recovered to $4,662
signals.src: World Gold Council / Kitco / China Daily
summary: Gold settled $4,661.80 on 27 Aug (+1.38%) after slipping to $4,598.20 on the hot July inflation print
Central banks bought a record 289 tonnes in Q2 2026
China's central bank added 15 tonnes in June, its largest month since October 2023
That takes first-half purchases to just over 40 tonnes and holdings to 2,346 tonnes across twenty consecutive months
signals.assessment: The 15-tonne and 40-tonne figures carried as a disagreement since 23 August are a monthly number and a half-year number. They agree, and the trace closes.

signals.headline: Thirty-nine US banking groups are building a shared stablecoin blockchain
summary: Thirty-nine US banking groups have formed a BankChain alliance to build shared stablecoin infrastructure
JPMorgan, Bank of America, Wells Fargo and Santander are separately exploring a global stablecoin consortium
Florida became the first US state to pass a stablecoin regulatory bill
The GENIUS Act rulemaking missed its statutory deadline and the CLARITY Act remains stalled
signals.assessment: The incumbent payment system deciding to own the issuance layer is a different answer to the scaling question than the one this has been watching for, and it arrives while the federal statute goes nowhere.

signals.headline: Spain drafted rules requiring data centres to source 80% of their power from new renewables, hour by hour
signals.src: Renewables Now / Data Center Dynamics / BeBeez
summary: Draft Spanish rules would require hourly matching against newly built renewable capacity
US data-centre moratoriums have now spread to 18 states
Alberta's data-centre ambitions are running into a global gas-turbine shortage
Siemens Energy is divesting its industrial unit to concentrate on gas turbines and grids
signals.assessment: A rule that forces load to arrive with its own generation attached is bad for a developer and good for turbines, switchgear and on-site storage. The two keep being read as one thing.

signals.headline: Romania drew its first EUR 2.5bn under the EU's SAFE instrument as European orders broadened
signals.src: PubAffairs Bruxelles / Defence Industry Europe / UK Defence Journal
summary: Romania received its first EUR 2.5bn payment under the SAFE defence instrument
Latvia is building a $233m explosives plant near the Russian border
Britain is expanding munitions capacity, with weapons and fighting-vehicle employment up 51%
Germany cancelled the F126 frigate programme in favour of Meko A-200 vessels
signals.assessment: European orders are broadening across countries and down the supply chain while the primes' share prices stay well below their highs - Rheinmetall is still about 26% off.

signals.headline: Canada awarded Chantier Davie C$11.3bn for six polar icebreakers, the largest such contract in Quebec's history
signals.src: Prime Minister of Canada / gCaptain / Splash247
summary: C$11.3bn (about $8.2bn) for six Polar Class 3 Canadian Coast Guard icebreakers, announced 24 Aug at Levis
Construction from 2027, first vessel five years later, full series in service by 2038
About 5,000 construction jobs and roughly C$650m a year of Canadian GDP
BAE Systems separately took up to $180m for USS Boxer modernisation
signals.assessment: Capacity is arriving without answering the question this item tracks: no award has yet used the 14 August memorandum permitting foreign construction of US Navy vessels, and Davie is privately held.

signals.headline: Unitree shed more than RMB 200bn of value in its first trading week after a 460% debut
summary: Unitree lost more than RMB 200bn of market value in its first week as analysts questioned the rating
Reuters' assessment: Chinese humanoids are not yet capable enough to take most jobs
XPeng's robotics business raised $900m at a $6.3bn valuation
The London robotaxi launch has slipped amid uncertainty at Transport for London
signals.assessment: Persistence beyond a debut week is one of two things this needs before it could be more than a watch item, and it is the one currently failing.

signals.headline: American Water set out about $48bn of planned system upgrades as the cluster's price leg was measured
summary: American Water plans about $48bn of water-system upgrades; Veralto agreed to buy Cleanwater for $465m
Dated 26 Aug closes: Ecolab $290.60 (-6.0% from its high), Trane $463.40 (-8.4%), Veralto $98.69 (-10.2%)
Xylem remains roughly 26% below its own high and is the sole cluster laggard
CISA reported more than 100 internet-exposed water systems attacked in July; Thames Water's drought pilot produced a surge in PFAS
signals.assessment: The price leg is now measured across four names on dated closes rather than asserted from one. One laggard against three near their highs is not cluster leadership.

signals.headline: EuroHPC selected thirteen European quantum-processor startups for its Grand Challenge
signals.src: Quantum Computing Report / HPCwire / The Quantum Insider
summary: Thirteen European QPU startups selected, including Sparrow Quantum on the photonic track
IBM completed its acquisition of HRL Laboratories
The National Science Foundation awarded $37.5m each to a Yale-led error-correction centre and an Illinois-led modular centre
BTIG publicly questioned IBM's 19 August modular-cooling milestone and the shares fell
signals.assessment: The first coordinated European hardware programme this category has recorded, and a route that does not depend on the US names - but it is public funding rather than an investible basket.

signals.headline: A US roadmap now targets fusion deployment by the mid-2030s
summary: The roadmap targets deployment by the mid-2030s - a government timetable rather than a research budget
Germany is planning what would be Europe's first commercial fusion power plant
General Fusion has traded on Nasdaq as GFUZ since 13 July with about $150m of cash
Britain's Tokamak Energy expanded high-temperature superconducting magnet capacity; Thea Energy extended its Series B
signals.assessment: Eighteen items across the week, the thinnest domain tracked, and two of them were real. The recirculating '$4bn raised' Commonwealth Fusion headline restates a 30 July close and is still not new money.

signals.headline: The FDA approved the first targeted therapy for metastatic pancreatic cancer
summary: Rasonque (daraxonrasib), from Revolution Medicines, approved 26 Aug ahead of schedule
A RAS inhibitor targeting a mutation present in more than 90% of pancreatic cancers
Median overall survival of 13.2 months in the second line against 6.7 months on standard chemotherapy
Separately, the Merck and Moderna phase 3 individualised melanoma vaccine readout of 19 August stands unchanged
signals.assessment: A landmark in one of oncology's hardest indications. Recorded as adjacent to the computationally designed medicine case rather than scored into it, because whether the molecule was computationally designed is not established.

signals.headline: Principal opened its 401(k) plans to private markets
summary: Principal, a major US retirement recordkeeper, has opened its 401(k) plans to private markets
Victory Capital agreed to acquire First Eagle for $7bn
The ECB committed central bank money to tokenised settlement with its Pontes launch
The CFA Institute says regulation has not kept pace with private credit's retail expansion
signals.assessment: A recordkeeper opening its plans is the step before money moves rather than the money moving. The Supreme Court hears Anderson v. Intel on 6 October and will not decide before mid-2027.

signals.headline: Apple shipped its first 2nm chip and AWS and Nvidia expanded their infrastructure partnership
signals.src: Jon Peddie Research / About Amazon / Qualcomm
summary: Apple shipped its first 2-nanometre chip (26 Aug)
AWS and Nvidia expanded their partnership for next-generation AI infrastructure
Qualcomm released IMSDK 2.0, a unified accelerated AI and multimedia toolkit
Samsung is reported to be moving AI compute into DRAM with a drop-in part that triples inference - single trade source, logged not scored
signals.assessment: Three more dated, vendor-sourced launches following the two that revived this on 25 August. Every named beneficiary is a large diversified company for which edge inference is a line rather than a business.

signals.headline: US-Canada aluminium talks are reported to have failed, leaving the 50% tariff in place
summary: Talks reported to have failed with the 50% tariff intact
Most US aluminium comes from Canada and the industry says replacing it is not realistic
COMEX copper set a fresh record on 25 Aug at $6.7125/lb on tariff-related warehouse positioning
CATL debuted an EV battery with a six-minute recharge
signals.assessment: The tariff outcome is single-sourced from a weak outlet and is logged rather than scored; the Canadian dependence behind it is corroborated and is the part that matters.

signals.headline: Nothing met the bar for a second consecutive cycle, on about 190 items
summary: About 190 items available across the week; the strongest were conglomerate revenue lines
Larsen and Toubro won a 6GWh battery engineering order in the Middle East; Adani took a Rs 4,700 crore Maharashtra transmission project
Insurers are publicly warning developers that cover is being arranged too late
The 21 August Saudi award stands: SAR 4.35bn for 2,000MW over four hours, split ACWA Power/Saudi Energy/Al Sharif and ENGIE
signals.assessment: A large sample with nothing that clears the bar is a finding rather than an absence. The basket problem - conglomerate revenue lines rather than pure plays - is the same one that keeps this off the main list.

signals.headline: Nothing met the bar for a ninth consecutive cycle, on 151 items
summary: 151 items across the week; the largest corporate item was John Deere's $10m investment in Reservoir Farms
Breedr plans expansion after a $27m raise; VitalFluid raised $19.9m Series A
No dated price catalyst at the listed names
China's new agricultural strategy emphasises domestic production over imports
signals.assessment: A ninth cycle with nothing clearing the bar, on a sample large enough that the silence is real rather than a gap in coverage.

signals.headline: Nothing met the bar for a fifth consecutive cycle, on 35 items
summary: 35 items across the week, one of the three thinnest domains tracked
Senior FDA officials and ARPA-H will lead a regulatory and clinical-trial session
L'Oreal and NUS Medicine signed a multi-million dollar healthy-ageing partnership
No dated price catalyst at any listed name
signals.assessment: The next real catalyst remains the ARDD conference in October. Thin coverage here is a known collection weakness and is logged separately.

signals.headline: The cluster's drawdown held for a fourth cycle with no dated catalyst
summary: Boston Scientific remains roughly 52% below its 52-week high on repeated 2026 guidance cuts and securities litigation
Intuitive Surgical is about 38% below its own high
Only Edwards Lifesciences and Dexcom sit near their highs
The FDA approved a wearable that simultaneously measures glucose and a second analyte
signals.assessment: Held for a fourth cycle and still well short of the promotion bar. A single device clearance does not answer a cluster-wide price failure.

signals.headline: A $1bn US facility is targeting 100-megajoule fusion output
summary: A $1bn US facility targets 100-megajoule output in a race with China
Valiant Products expanded metal additive manufacturing capacity
A pure-lithium battery cell passed 9,315 cycles
No dated listed-company catalyst in the week's 117 items
signals.assessment: The week's real content in this domain belongs to fusion rather than to advanced materials as a standalone case. Nothing here clears the bar on its own.

signals.headline: Prediction markets drew congressional scrutiny as the IPO pipeline stayed regional
summary: Congress is examining ethics and regulatory gaps in prediction markets; Kalshi pulled a market amid a staffer controversy
Five MLB teams partnered with Kalshi, testing Polymarket's exclusivity
Unique X is exploring a London listing as UK tech listings seek a revival
India's IPO pipeline hit a record Rs 4.72 lakh crore with 239 firms lining up
signals.assessment: The listings activity is concentrated in India and the regulatory activity in US prediction markets; neither yet changes what a UK or European reader can access.

signals.headline: Brent's third straight down session breaks the escalation pattern, on softer sanctions and Iran-Oman corridor talks
summary: Brent fell from $94.39 (21 Aug) to a one-week low around $88-90 (25 Aug) to roughly $86-87 (26 Aug)
Treasury's 24 Aug sanctions round deliberately excluded immediate secondary sanctions on Iran's trading partners, per Bessent's own 'cure period' language
Iran and Oman are reported to have agreed the coordinates of an interim two-way Hormuz shipping corridor (25-26 Aug)
signals.assessment: Three consecutive down sessions on a named, specific mechanism is a genuinely two-sided challenge; conviction on the energy-premium call is cut from 5 to 4.

signals.headline: Samsung states a KRW 90-110tn 2026 shareholder-return range; the market sold memory anyway
summary: Samsung's own figure replaces a spread of unusable prior estimates ($80bn / KRW 110tn / $101bn)
Micron fell 7%, SK hynix 5%, SanDisk 9%, Seagate and Western Digital 7% on 24 Aug on the absence of an immediate buyback
TrendForce (25 Aug) sizes memory at roughly 68% of major cloud providers' 2027 capital spending
signals.assessment: Read as a capital-return disappointment, not a supply or pricing invalidation - TrendForce's forecasts keep revising upward.

signals.headline: AAOI's $600m at-the-market equity raise is a distinct dilution catalyst, not a Fabrinet echo
summary: 21 Aug SEC 8-K: AAOI entered a $600m at-the-market distribution agreement with Raymond James and Needham
Its third capital raise of 2026; shares fell about 10% to $112.11 the same day, then to $107.63 by 24 Aug
signals.assessment: Corrects the prior framing of AAOI's continued fall as merely a continuation of the 18 Aug Fabrinet cut.

signals.headline: GE Vernova's Q2 2026 8-K, read directly, confirms $16.7bn of Power orders and $6.3bn of Electrification orders
summary: Power segment orders $16.7bn, +134% organic; Electrification orders $6.3bn, +66% organic, on $3.6bn of Electrification revenue
116GW gas-power backlog plus slot reservations, $24.2bn total Q2 orders, $176bn total company backlog
More than 500 local data-centre moratorium instruments now exist across 42 US states
signals.assessment: Closes a trace open since 23 Aug on the primary filing text; the curtailment map is wider than the headline states already carried.

signals.headline: Rheinmetall's YTD figure corrected to about -26%, closing a six-run-old trace
summary: Two independent sources converge on roughly -26% year to date and about 26% below the 52-week high
Replaces the -39.6%/-42% figures, which rested on an inference about when the 52-week high was set
A $1.5tn FY27 US defence budget request, $331bn for munitions, went to Congress 22-25 Aug
signals.assessment: Closes the standing price-provenance trace on RHM.DE; the wider supplier-base evidence is additive to the 24 Aug single-issuer correction.

signals.headline: Rocket Lab has fallen to about $67-70, roughly 55% off its late-May high, reversing the prior session's rebound
summary: Down from the ~$83 level carried 24 Aug; order-book evidence (Viasat, Intuitive Machines, Iridium) is unchanged and strong
A Neutron first-stage tank test failure is cited by secondary sources as the cause of a renewed delay, pending a primary source
signals.assessment: The order book and the share price are now tracked as separate legs rather than one arrow.

signals.headline: CISA adds a maximum-severity Oracle flaw, exploited since January, to its exploited catalogue
summary: CVE-2026-21962 (Oracle HTTP Server/WebLogic proxy plug-in), CVSS 10.0, unauthenticated and network-exploitable
Added to CISA's KEV catalogue 24 Aug with a 27 Aug federal remediation deadline
signals.assessment: A third live enterprise vector this month; still threat rather than spend ahead of tonight's CrowdStrike print.

signals.headline: Bitcoin's 25 Aug session settled near $78,586, correcting an $80,704 intraday snapshot
summary: Opened $78,982, spiked intraday to $81,023, then gave the gain back to settle near $78,586 - essentially flat on the week
Ether ETF inflows added a separate $697m over the week
signals.assessment: Corrects a snapshot-as-close read; conviction is unchanged at 4 on flows and rulemaking, not on the settled price move.

signals.headline: Lynas posts record FY26 results as MP Materials pulls back 4.4%
summary: Lynas FY26 (ASX primary): record revenue A$977.9m, NPAT A$222.4m, NdPr output +11% to 7,260t at $80.7/kg average realised price
MP Materials closed $57.66 on 25 Aug, down 4.4% on the day after $60.31 on 24 Aug
Ex-China NdPr below its $110/kg floor now confirmed by two independent price assessors
signals.assessment: MP's pullback is a level, not a reversal of the domain's two-sided case; Lynas is the first hard non-US comparator print this run.

signals.headline: Westinghouse's confidential IPO filing is now independently dated to 31 July 2026
signals.src: Axios / Yahoo Finance / Nuclear Engineering International
summary: Confidential Form S-1 draft submitted to the SEC 31 July 2026; owned 49% Cameco/51% Brookfield Renewable

signals.assessment: The bounce is recorded against a >36% YTD drawdown as an oversold move, not a reversal of the 23 Aug conviction cut.

signals.headline: A UCITS humanoid-robotics fund has traded in London since October 2025, correcting a standing access claim
summary: The KraneShares Global Humanoid & Embodied Intelligence UCITS ETF (LSE: KOID) has traded since 9 Oct 2025
Roundhill's HUMN has traded on Cboe since mid-2025; both are non-China-specific
Neither is a pure humanoid-maker basket - both carry meaningful weight in enablers and adjacent industrials
signals.assessment: Corrects the humanoid radar item's claim that no usable basket exists; does not itself trigger a promotion.

signals.headline: Edge-AI revives on two dated product launches after nine consecutive quiet cycles
summary: NVIDIA launched the Jetson Orin Nano 2 (25 Aug), with Cognex and Aptiv both confirming support the same day
Apple launched M6/M5 Max/M5 Ultra chips (25 Aug), explicitly framed around AI compute
signals.assessment: Both meet the domain's own stated revival bar - a dated product launch with a named listed beneficiary - after the prior nine cycles found none.

signals.headline: Xanadu (XNDU) is a third quantum basket constituent missed, alongside Quantinuum and IQM
summary: Xanadu has traded on Nasdaq/TSX since 27 March 2026 (~$302m raised via SPAC merger)
NSF committed $290m across eight quantum research institutes, 25 Aug
signals.assessment: Basket re-verification obligation closes with a third missed constituent; held at 3 of 5 as the pure-play cluster extended its price drawdown.

signals.headline: Nscale's targeted US listing sharpens to 'as early as September, up to $3bn'
summary: Prior 'preparing a listing' framing now carries a specific month and size
CRWV/NBIS/IREN fell in sympathy on 24 Aug
signals.assessment: A dated catalyst behind this week's neocloud weakness; no change to the theme's conviction.

signals.headline: COMEX copper sets a fresh record as tariff-related positioning moves metal into US warehouses
summary: September copper settled +1.6% at $6.7125/lb on 25 Aug, surpassing the prior 12 Aug record
LME copper reached $14,343/t, near its own record, on 65,400t of warehouse withdrawals
signals.assessment: A genuine cluster price-leadership signal for the metals leg of the reshoring driver.

signals.headline: The new Canadian auto tariff is a separate, later instrument than the Section 338 duties already in force
summary: Trump's 24 Aug announcement raises Canadian auto, truck and steel tariffs from a 25% baseline to 50%, effective 1 Jan 2027
This is layered alongside, not stacked onto, the Section 338 50% duties in force on other goods since 22 Aug
signals.assessment: Corrects a driver oneLiner that risked being read as an immediate stack to a higher combined rate.

signals.headline: Xylem re-confirmed as the one cluster laggard, still about 26% below its 52-week high
summary: Xylem $113.85 (24 Aug), essentially unchanged from the 18 Aug level already carried
Trane, Ecolab and Veralto were not independently re-pulled this run - carried as a residual gap
signals.assessment: Nothing new met the bar this week beyond routine local PFAS settlement-credit coverage.

signals.headline: Moderna's actual reaction to the melanoma-vaccine readout was a 177% intraday spike, not a flat 8% gain
summary: Moderna spiked +177% intraday on 19 Aug, gave back 20-25% the next session, closed 25 Aug at $156.75 - about 2.5x its pre-announcement level
Merck rose 12.5% on 19 Aug and traded 24 Aug within about 1% of a fresh 52-week high
signals.assessment: Corrects an understated price-leg reading; the filing/second-sponsor criteria remain unmet, so the score stays at 2 of 5.

signals.headline: The Bank of England's 30 July dissenters are named: Greene, Mann and Pill voted for a rise
summary: 6-3 hold at 3.75%, the most hawkish split since 2016
Next decision scheduled 17 Sept, the same week as the Fed
signals.assessment: Detail addition to a standing hawkish read; no conviction change.

signals.headline: A new ADP weekly payrolls series shows soft, not-yet-turning private hiring
summary: Average weekly private-payroll gains of 11,750 across the four weeks to 8 Aug
The BLS preliminary benchmark revision (28 Aug) covers March 2026 state-level data only, not a national NFP correction
signals.assessment: Consistent with stasis rather than a turn; the early-September payroll print remains the real test.

signals.headline: Korea partly repairs to 6,742.74 while Japan diverges further upward
summary: KOSPI +0.68% to 6,742.74 on 25 Aug, still about 28% below its June 2026 record
Nikkei roughly +33% year to date, the sharper ex-US signal this week
signals.assessment: A bounce, not a reversal of the standing Korea deterioration.

signals.headline: US Treasury sanctions ~60 Iran-linked entities and vessels, and Brent fell instead of rising
signals.src: US Treasury (home.treasury.gov) / CNN / Axios / Al Jazeera
summary: OFAC's 24 August action, framed by Secretary Bessent as "Operation Economic Outcast", targets roughly sixty entities, individuals and shadow-fleet vessels across the UAE, Hong Kong, China, Singapore and Switzerland
The network is accused of moving Iranian oil revenue to the Revolutionary Guard's Quds Force; Iran has vowed "seismic" retaliation
Brent fell to $92.17 on 24 August and $91.78 by Tuesday morning, a second straight decline through the escalation
signals.assessment: Every prior escalation this month moved the price up. This one did not, which is worth watching against the entry's high conviction rather than explaining away.

signals.headline: The 24 August gold figure was a snapshot, not a close; the settled level is $4,640.80
summary: Monday's page carried $4,694.90, the 06:00Z snapshot on a 24-hour market
The settled 24 August close is $4,640.80, independently confirmed against the COMEX benchmark
Tuesday's level is $4,695.20, +1.17% on the corrected prior close, still about 16% below the January peak
signals.assessment: The same snapshot-versus-close gap seen before on Brent and Korea. It does not change the recovery's direction.

signals.headline: US-Canada tariff talks collapsed into 50% duties and dollar-for-dollar retaliation
summary: Talks over heavy-duty-truck tariff relief collapsed 21-22 August; the US imposed 50% tariffs on about $20bn of Canadian autos, parts, steel and trucks from 22 August
Canada set dollar-for-dollar retaliation on US steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper and electronics, effective 8 September
On 24 August Washington threatened to double car and truck tariffs on Canada to 50% from 2027
signals.assessment: An escalation, not the rollback that yesterday's coverage of the same talks suggested.

signals.headline: USA Rare Earth completes a $1.55bn government-backed financing for a Brazilian rare-earth mine
summary: The upsized SPV funds an offtake of 100% of Phase 1 production from Serra Verde's ionic-clay mine, the only such mine in commercial production outside Asia
Structure: a $750m Department of War investment, a $500m Tier-1 bank revolving credit facility, and $300m-plus of government forward-purchase contracts over five years
Shareholder vote on the deal is scheduled for 28 August; shares fell about 5% on the announcement despite the milestone
signals.assessment: The first concrete listed capital-flow signal behind the western rare-earth supply chain specifically, distinct from the tariff-instrument leg of reshoring.

signals.headline: SK hynix's own earnings call confirms it dropped long-term contract price caps; Samsung's 20% target stays unconfirmed
signals.src: SK hynix Q2 2026 earnings call (29 Jul) / BigGo / TrendForce
summary: SK hynix disclosed on its own 29 July call that it completed long-term agreement negotiations with about ten customers without the traditional price cap
Samsung has issued no official comment on a reported ~20% Q3 DRAM price target; every account traces to unnamed customer notifications
Separately, AI-server builders serving Microsoft, Google and Oracle notified customers of price rises above 15% on next-generation systems (Bloomberg, 22 Aug)
signals.assessment: One half of a trade-press claim logged five days ago is now company-confirmed; the other half stays unconfirmed. The memory shortage has moved into finished-system pricing either way.

signals.headline: Applied Optoelectronics fell a further 14% in three sessions, extending the post-Fabrinet correction
summary: AAOI closed $124.82 on 22 August, down 16.9% from its 14 August level, and $107.63 by 25 August
The move is a continuation of the correction that began with Fabrinet's 18 August selloff on a record quarter
The demand record behind the theme is unaffected; the price leg that justified confirmed status is falling for a second consecutive week
signals.assessment: A level, not a headline count, and it argues for a trajectory cut rather than a stabilisation.

signals.headline: The EU approved EUR 6.1bn of new Ukraine defence procurement, spread across suppliers
summary: Approved 24 August, Ukraine's Independence Day, drawn from the EU's EUR 90bn loan
Covers air and missile defence systems, missiles, ammunition and radars
Procurement is spread across EU defence companies rather than concentrated in one national champion
signals.assessment: A broadening of the European rearmament capital flow already visible in Germany and the UK, on a different axis to any single company's order book.

signals.headline: Bosch commits to an August 2027 humanoid production line; Tesla confirms a Cybercab event for 3 September
summary: Bosch will begin mass-producing humanoid robots at its Buhl, Germany plant in August 2027, partnered with UK startup Humanoid; Schaeffler is an early customer
The first Europe-based humanoid production line reported to date
Tesla sent direct rider invites for a Cybercab production-launch event in Austin on 3 September, extending its existing limited driverless service
signals.assessment: Geographic broadening of the humanoid build-out rather than a new listed vehicle; access remains the binding constraint, not evidence.

signals.headline: Australia warns of active exploitation of a critical TeamCity authentication-bypass flaw
summary: CVE-2026-63077, CVSS 9.8, permits authentication bypass and remote code execution on TeamCity On-Premises
Alert published 24 August and adds to the week's Clop/Windchill breach and AI-directed attacks on industrial controllers
CrowdStrike reports 26 August and Palo Alto Networks 1 September - the two prints that will show whether this threat evidence converts into spend
signals.assessment: Another primary-sourced addition to the strongest week of threat evidence this category has produced; the budget question is still unanswered.

signals.headline: Korea's KOSPI fell a second straight session to its lowest close of the move
signals.src: Korea Times / Sedaily / Asia Business Daily
summary: The KOSPI settled 6,696.96 on 24 August, down 3.12%, chip-led (Samsung, SK Hynix) ahead of Nvidia's earnings
Now about 29% below the 9,385.59 June 2026 record, reversing part of the prior week's partial repair

China's RMB 800bn (~$119bn) financing instrument opened to local-authority applications around 24 August - the first actual instrument after four cycles of pledges, though deployment is expected to take at least another month
signals.assessment: Korea's repair did not hold, which is worth carrying against last week's more optimistic framing rather than smoothing over.

signals.headline: Taiwan indicts nine, including Nvidia and Super Micro staff, over alleged smuggling of AI servers to China
summary: Keelung District Prosecutors indicted nine people, widened from three, over roughly 50 Super Micro servers loaded with Nvidia chips allegedly routed to China via Japan on falsified paperwork
At least some units passed Taiwan customs before being re-routed; the chips are the class subject to US export controls in force since 2022
Taiwan's first openly acknowledged enforcement action of this kind, after Washington had pushed the island to police the route
signals.assessment: An enforcement action on the transhipment route rather than a new control -- it tests compliance on paper rules already in place, and it is dated evidence rather than a policy change.

signals.headline: Brent slipped below $93 on Monday morning ahead of the US sanctions announcement on Iran
summary: Brent fell about 1.3% to $93.20 after two consecutive weekly gains of roughly 6%
Washington is due to detail sanctions aimed at Iran's trading partners today, and Goldman Sachs argues the disruption was already in the price
Washington has separately eased some Russian oil sanctions to cap the increase, to European unease
signals.assessment: The first instrument pointing the other way in six weeks is an American one, and it is aimed at the price rather than at the conflict.

signals.headline: Washington details its Iran sanctions package today as Beijing refuses to join it
summary: The Treasury Secretary said on 20 August that the measures would be the toughest in history and aimed at Iran's trading partners
China has rejected the US demand to join and Iran has vowed a devastating response to any attempt to cut its economic lifelines
The Senate passed sweeping Russian energy sanctions 86-11 in the same stretch, with 100% tariffs on buyers of Russian oil
signals.assessment: Secondary sanctions close the adaptation route from the other side, which strengthens the premium and raises its tail risk at once.

signals.headline: Gold reached $4,695, the high of its recovery and 16% short of the January record
summary: $4,694.90 at 06:00Z on 24 August, up 1.53%, against $4,654.66 spot four hours earlier
+17.3% against the $4,001 of 14 July and the best month since January; the record is $5,597.23 on 29 January 2026
China's central bank bought 40 tonnes in June, its second-largest month since early 2025, and the Bank of Korea is buying again
signals.assessment: A recovery at the high of its move with official buying underneath it, and the peak of January still four hundred dollars above.

signals.headline: The Bank for International Settlements named circular financing in AI infrastructure as a repricing risk
summary: The warning pairs high valuations with circular financing structures, and says capital spending is approaching cash-flow limits
About $194bn of AI-related bond issuance is straining the debt market; Morgan Stanley sees hyperscaler capex up 57% in 2027
Bank of America raised its cumulative hyperscaler figure to $3.6tn through 2028
signals.assessment: An international body has now used the same words as the stated condition that would break the capex case, which is not the same as the condition firing.

signals.headline: SK hynix removes long-term contract price caps and Samsung targets a further ~20% on Q3 DRAM prices
summary: Both makers are shortening contract lengths and moving to post-settlement pricing that lets a price adjust after delivery
Both describe 2026 HBM, DRAM and NAND capacity as essentially sold out; both are running 40-50% operating margins
TrendForce's 9 July release put 3Q26 server DRAM up 13-18% q/q with long-term agreements credited for capping the increase - the cap is the part reported to have gone
signals.assessment: If it holds up against a company source, the one structural brake in view has been removed. It rests on trade press for now and nothing moves on it yet.

signals.headline: Jackson Hole runs 27-29 August and Kevin Warsh gives his first keynote as Fed chair on the 28th
signals.src: Kansas City Fed symposium programme via market previews
summary: The symposium is held at Jackson Lake Lodge, Wyoming, with about 120 central bankers from more than 70 countries attending
The 2026 theme is financial innovation and its implications for payments and policy

Warsh, sworn in 22 May, told reporters after the 29 July meeting that he wants the speech to frame the big questions rather than signal near-term policy; 69% of surveyed fund managers expect a neutral tone
signals.assessment: It lands two days after NVIDIA reports and nineteen days before the 16 September FOMC, which makes it the largest scheduled input into the September path between now and the decision.

signals.headline: Bitcoin's best week since 2024 came with about $1.6bn of spot ETF inflows behind it
summary: Bitcoin settled 21 August at $78,335, up 7.26% on the session, with an intraday high near $79,500
Roughly $1.6bn of spot ETF inflows on the week, with BlackRock taking 83% of one $606m inflow day, alongside billions of forced short liquidations and a weaker dollar
It eased to about $77,000 over the weekend with the ETF bid paused
signals.assessment: The flows leg of this case is evidenced for the first time. Set against it, separate coverage describes investors continuing to pull billions while the statute stalls; the two measure different windows and neither is adopted over the other.

signals.headline: Record second-quarter central-bank gold buying of 288.9 tonnes, against the weakest half since 2022
signals.src: World Gold Council, Gold Demand Trends Q2 2026
summary: Q2 net central-bank purchases 288.9 tonnes, +62% from 177.9t a year earlier - the highest second quarter on record, bought into a quarter when gold fell ~16%
National Bank of Poland the largest buyer at 51t in Q2 and 82t across H1, toward a self-set ~700t target; PBoC also adding; Turkish and Russian sales slowing
BUT H1 2026 central-bank demand is only ~345 tonnes - the WEAKEST half-year since 2022. The record quarter is catch-up after a very weak Q1
signals.assessment: Confirmed against the World Gold Council's own Gold Demand Trends and corroborated independently: a net 288.9 tonnes in Q2, up 62% year on year, the strongest second quarter on record, bought into a quarter when gold fell about 16%, with Poland the largest buyer at 51 tonnes. The H1 total of about 345 tonnes is the weakest half-year since 2022, so the record quarter is catch-up rather than acceleration.

signals.headline: Nvidia told hyperscalers AI server prices rise more than 15% from early 2027
summary: Applies to Vera Rubin and Grace Blackwell systems; the first Vera Rubin machines have gone to Microsoft
Nvidia is separately reported to have locked multi-year memory supply with Micron
Morgan Stanley sees DDR4 up 50% in the third quarter and top-five NAND revenue rose 77% sequentially in the second
signals.assessment: Memory cost is now visible in the price of the finished machine, which is as far up the stack as this can travel.

signals.headline: TrendForce revised its DRAM forecasts up rather than down
summary: 3Q26 PC DRAM contract prices revised UP from +8-13% to +15-20% q/q; 4Q26 from +0-5% to +3-8%
The 9 July release gives 13-18% q/q for SERVER DRAM in 3Q26, with long-term agreements capping increases - previously cited as 'conventional DRAM, 13 Aug'
SanDisk FQ4 revenue +371.6% y/y at an 84.6% GAAP gross margin; Western Digital FQ4 +43.8% at a 54.4% non-GAAP gross margin
signals.assessment: Conventional DRAM pricing is being revised UP into end-2026 while CXMT's funded expansion is a 2027 event. The supply fact stands; the near-term shortage is intensifying. Conviction unchanged at 4.

signals.headline: MP Materials ran from about $38 on 29 July to about $60.06 on 21 August, but only 2.26% of it in that final week
summary: MP ~$38 on 29 July to $60.05 on 21 August, +23.5% in the past week; Friday USA Rare Earth +8%, Critical Metals +10%, MP +5%
MP Q2 revenue $108.49m, +89% y/y, beating $95.95m consensus by 13%; Morgan Stanley target to $73, Overweight; Q3 NdPr guided >1,000t at high-$90s/kg; first GM magnet shipments Q4 2026
The G7 agreed at Evian on 17 JUNE 2026 that no single country supply more than 60% of rare-earth and magnet imports by 2030, then 50%
signals.assessment: Q2 revenue $108.49m, up 89% and 12% above a $96.9m consensus; Q3 guidance above 1,000 tonnes of NdPr at realised pricing in the high $90s per kilogram, with Pentagon price support underwriting it. Morgan Stanley raised its target to $73 at overweight; Deutsche Bank and JPMorgan trimmed targets and kept buy ratings.

signals.headline: Nebius expects more than $9bn of customer prepayments in 2026; IREN's $3.4bn NVIDIA deal is dated 7 May
signals.src: Nebius Q2 shareholder letter (SEC 6-K) / IREN IR, GlobeNewswire
summary: Nebius, 12 August: expects over $9bn of customer prepayments in 2026 alongside asset-backed financing, corporate debt and an ATM programme
From the same letter: 'We could sell our entire 2027 capacity on these terms today. We are deliberately not doing so.'
IREN's five-year $3.4bn NVIDIA AI-cloud contract is dated 7 May 2026 - air-cooled Blackwell within ~60MW at Childress, Texas - three and a half months old
signals.assessment: Both were recorded and unassessed yesterday for want of a date. One is fresh and one is not, and the standard that separated them was applied before either was known to help or hurt.

signals.headline: Optical interconnect is up hard on the year: AAOI about +216%, Coherent and Lumentum both doubled
summary: 19 Aug: Coherent +16% to $422, Lumentum +13% through $1,024, Applied Optoelectronics +8%. 12 Aug: LITE +15% on a blowout FQ4, COHR +9%
4 Aug: AAOI +17%, COHR +11%, LITE +6% on a Reuters report of US restrictions on Chinese optical transceivers. Cumulative: AAOI +76% in nine sessions, COHR +48%
NVIDIA's $4bn photonics investment - $2bn each into Lumentum and Coherent - is dated 2 March 2026, not August
signals.assessment: Dated August legs: 4 August AAOI +17%, COHR +10%, LITE +9% on a reported US restriction of Chinese transceivers; 7 August AAOI +13%, COHR +13%, LITE +8% on AAOI's print; 12 August LITE +15%; 19 August COHR +16% and LITE +13%. It cuts both ways - on 10 August COHR fell 12% and LITE 7% on valuation. AAOI guides above $1bn of 2026 sales.

signals.headline: The $5bn of first-half data-centre electrification orders belongs to GE Vernova
summary: GE Vernova booked ~$5bn of data-centre power equipment orders in H1 2026, more than double its entire 2025 total, with $2.7bn in Q2 alone
Morgan Stanley's 38 GW gap is corroborated across four outlets with a consistent decomposition: ~68 GW of need 2026-28, ~15 GW building, ~15 GW available or contracted
Grid interconnection now takes five to seven years in parts of the US; MS's named fixes include converting former bitcoin-mining sites with existing power
signals.assessment: GE Vernova booked about $5bn of data-centre electrification orders in H1, more than twice full-year 2025, and the split now reconciles arithmetically as $2.4bn in Q1 plus $2.7bn in Q2. The Eaton attribution is not supported.

signals.headline: The 16 September FOMC carries a ~69% chance of no change and ~31% of a 25bp increase
summary: Polymarket prices the 16 September FOMC at 69% no change / 31% +25bp / ~1.3% cut, read 22 August
CME FedWatch readings give 67.6% HOLD on 13 August and 68.4% HOLD on 20 August, target 3.50-3.75%
The 60.1%/78.8% HIKE figures in circulation are dated 29 July - FOMC day - and fell that afternoon as Warsh spoke
signals.assessment: Instrument readings rather than commentary: Polymarket 69/31 on 22 August, CME FedWatch 67.6% and 68.4% for a hold on 13 and 20 August, target 3.50-3.75%. The 60.1%/78.8% increase readings in circulation are dated 29 July, FOMC day, and fell that afternoon. Friday's tape agrees: equities up, volatility down 5.50%, crypto's best week since 2024.

signals.headline: Canada set 8 September for dollar-for-dollar counter-tariffs after talks collapsed
summary: US 50% duties took effect on about $20bn of Canadian goods on 22 August after negotiations broke down over Canadian demands for truck-tariff relief
Carney said Canada is 'at war' on trade and will match dollar for dollar from 8 September, targeting steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper and electronics
A proposed deal would have locked in 15% auto tariffs and 25% on steel; Ottawa is now preparing a relief plan for its own businesses
signals.assessment: Two of the six retaliation sectors are inputs to American industrial production, which is the first time the tariff instruments have cut against domestic industry here.

signals.headline: Canada sets 8 September for counter-tariffs on $20bn of US goods across six sectors
summary: Carney announced dollar-for-dollar counter-tariffs on $20bn of American products, effective 8 September 2026
Named sectors: steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics
Four outlets carry the $20bn scope on both sides, described as roughly 5% of what Canada ships to the US each year; talks are suspended and none are scheduled
signals.assessment: A threat on Friday now has an effective date, a value and a sector list. Two of the six sectors sit inside themes tracked here.

signals.headline: US-Canada talks collapsed at midnight and 50% Section 338 duties went live on about $20bn of goods
signals.src: NPR / NBC / Bloomberg / Al Jazeera / AP-syndicated
summary: Talks fell apart Friday night minutes before the deadline; duties took effect at the stroke of midnight on hockey sticks, building materials, liquors and certain clothing
USTR Jamieson Greer says Canadian negotiators made eleventh-hour demands that upended a draft deal; a point of contention was Canadian prohibitions on certain US goods and services
Carney suspended negotiations, recalled his team to Ottawa and said Canada 'will match those tariffs dollar for dollar'. No new talks are scheduled
signals.assessment: Duties took effect at 00:01 ET on hockey sticks, building materials, liquors and certain clothing. USTR Jamieson Greer says Canadian negotiators made eleventh-hour demands that upended a draft deal; Carney suspended talks and recalled his team. Four outlets put the scope at $20bn, about 5% of Canadian exports south.

signals.headline: Congress is legislating against the memorandum that opened US Navy shipbuilding to foreign yards
signals.src: USNI News / Navy Times / Defense Daily / Rep. Golden
summary: House FY27 NDAA, passed in July: bars foreign construction of warships AND combat-logistics vessels; no FY27 funds may be obligated for a battle-force ship built abroad
Senate SASC mark strips the Title 10 presidential 'national security interest' waiver, while permitting up to two AUXILIARY ships from foreign yards conditioned on US investment
Hanwha's 'first US Navy contract under MASGA' - an NGLS subcontract with Vard Marine US - is dated 30-31 MARCH 2026, five months before the memorandum
signals.assessment: The House FY27 NDAA, passed in July, bars foreign construction of warships and combat-logistics vessels and blocks FY27 funds for any battle-force ship built abroad. The Senate mark strips the presidential national-security waiver while allowing up to two auxiliaries from foreign yards conditioned on US investment. The White House protested on 24 July.

signals.headline: Hong Kong's listing boom passed $40bn and the humanoid pipeline is forming behind Unitree
summary: Hong Kong fundraising has topped $40bn and surpassed the 2025 total, with the exchange's own second-quarter profit up 21%
Chery's robot unit is weighing a listing, LimX is targeting $300m in Hong Kong and Nscale is preparing a $3bn US listing
SK hynix is preparing a US listing reported near $29.5bn and India's NSE has clearance for a September listing
signals.assessment: The primary market is where three of these themes' themes are getting their first tradeable prices, which is a route the coverage universe does not enumerate.

signals.headline: Bitcoin's best week since 2024 came with $1.6bn of spot ETF inflows behind it
summary: Settled $78,335 on 21 August after a $606m single-day inflow with BlackRock taking 83% of it, and about $2.7bn of short liquidations
Five consecutive inflow days totalled $1.67bn; $2.6bn went into bitcoin and ether funds across the week
Eased to $77,141 by 24 August with the fund bid paused over the weekend
signals.assessment: Measured money rather than a squeeze alone, which is the first time this has had a flows leg worth the name.

signals.headline: The CFTC begins exploring crypto rules while the CLARITY Act waits for the autumn
summary: The Senate procedural vote on the CLARITY Act ripens 15 September; Polymarket puts 2026 enactment near 15.5% against about 30% a week earlier
Bitcoin's rally topped $79,000 intraday on short covering and ETF inflows before easing
signals.assessment: A regulator writing rules is a narrower and slower route than a statute, but it does not need sixty senators. It is the only forward motion on the legislative leg in a month.

signals.headline: Iranian oil offers to Chinese buyers fall as the US blockade bites
summary: Sources describe fewer and lower offers reaching Chinese refiners
Brent settled $94.39 on 21 August, up 0.65% and about 6.4% over two weeks
The US Treasury details its sanctions package on Iran's trading partners on Monday 24 August
signals.assessment: The first evidence that the pressure campaign is working on physical flow rather than only on the risk premium. More than 660m barrels have still been escorted through Hormuz since early May, so this remains a premium rather than an outage.

signals.headline: Independent coverage confirms fusion's first publicly listed company
signals.src: The Globe and Mail / Pulse 2.0 / American Nuclear Society
summary: General Fusion has traded on Nasdaq as GFUZ since 13 July with about $150m of cash and gave its first public-company update on 18 August
LM26 has compressed plasma with a lithium liner to about 0.72 keV, roughly 8.4 million degrees, funded through the end of 2028
Pacific Fusion and Lawrence Livermore reached a 3,000-shot milestone on the Sirius prototype and Thea Energy extended its Series B
signals.assessment: Nine collected items across the week, the thinnest of any domain here, which is a question about collection breadth rather than about the subject.

signals.headline: Iran's president calls for an end to the war and defends the 17 June memorandum in parliament
signals.src: Al Jazeera / France 24 / Euronews / Gulf News
summary: Masoud Pezeshkian said on 21 August that it is time to end the months-long war while Tehran negotiates from a position of strength
He defended the 17 June 2026 memorandum of understanding with Washington against hardline critics: 'they cannot find even a single clause in this agreement that indicates capitulation'
The 60-day negotiating clock inside that memorandum expired on 17 August; the memorandum itself has not
signals.assessment: The first de-escalation signal in this file for weeks, and it arrives the day after the sanctions warning. The premium now has dated inputs pulling either way.

signals.headline: Gold's Friday settle is confirmed at $4,680.60, the highest level of the move
signals.src: COMEX December futures via Yahoo Finance and CNBC quote pages, 21 Aug 2026
summary: A gain of $109.20, or 2.39%, on the session; spot gold is quoted about 1.5% lower near $4,607
Still about 16% below the peak near $5,589-5,602 of 28 January 2026
Central banks bought a net 288.9 tonnes in the second quarter, a record second quarter, against about 345 tonnes for the half - the weakest half since 2022
signals.assessment: The best month since January, and still a recovery rather than a record run. The record quarter of official buying is catch-up after the weakest half in four years.

signals.headline: Beijing pledged fiscal support as growth slipped further below target
summary: A vice finance minister signalled more fiscal support on 21 August and the central bank pledged timely adjustment
Loan prime rates were unchanged at 3.00% and 3.50% for a fifteenth consecutive month on 20 August; a nine-department plan to lift county-level consumption was published on 18 August
Goldman Sachs flagged the stimulus risk as growth slips; July industrial output and retail sales both missed
signals.assessment: Four consecutive cycles of no policy at all have become pledges without instruments, which is a change and not yet an easing.

signals.headline: YMTC's parent seeks $4.9bn in a Shanghai listing, a month after CXMT's debut
summary: YMTC is China's leading NAND flash maker; CXMT raised about $8.56bn on the STAR Market on 27 July
A Korean court has separately heard that CXMT planned to use misappropriated Samsung process material
signals.assessment: The supply answer to the memory shortage is being capitalised on public markets. It does not trigger the entry's stated stated breaking condition, which is an average-selling-price rollover, but it funds the thing that eventually would.

signals.headline: Washington will back US minerals projects with $500m of grants
summary: Reported 21 August, alongside $162m awarded to recover critical minerals from mining waste
A $400m Defense Department loan commitment went to the Syerston scandium project and funding went to rare-earth work in four African countries
Tactical Resources began trading on Nasdaq on 20 August, adding a listed name to a thin basket
signals.assessment: Public money keeps arriving on the western side while the western price falls, which is the tension this category now runs on.

signals.headline: Vanguard published arithmetic against the private-equity pitch to retirement savers
summary: The largest provider of the retirement plans this depends on argues the return case does not survive fees and dispersion
The Bank of Canada separately flagged the growth of private credit as a financial-stability concern and restructuring questions are being asked of stressed credit
On the other side: CVC agreed a $3.5bn credit and secondaries partnership with AIG and Cox Capital pushed its tender-offer model into interval funds
signals.assessment: The distribution build and the objections to it arrived in the same four days, and the objections came from the two institutions best placed to slow it.

signals.headline: Tesla is reported approved for robotaxi service in Nevada, including Las Vegas
summary: Reported 21 August 2026 by a single enthusiast outlet; no regulator or company source has been found for it
It would follow Waymo running driver-out in Atlanta and clearance to expand across eighteen metropolitan areas
The humanoid side is unchanged: Optimus V3 is described as targeting low-volume Fremont production from summer 2026, consumer availability no earlier than end-2027
signals.assessment: Carried and not treated as a confirmation until a regulator source is found. Autonomy keeps clearing regulators while humanoids keep not clearing evidence.

signals.headline: Quantum's cluster rose hard on 21 August into a year-to-date drawdown
summary: Infleqtion +10%, Rigetti +9-10.5%, IonQ +7% to $44.62 on 21 August
Every established pure play entered that session down on the year: IonQ -7%, Rigetti -27%, D-Wave -28%
IonQ's Q2 was its largest ever - revenue $80.05m, +286.8% y/y, 20.5% above consensus, with FY2026 guidance raised to $280-290m; Rigetti tripled to about $5.1m
signals.assessment: A one-session cluster move inside a year-to-date drawdown is a bounce, not leadership. The revenue leg is now the strong one and the price leg is the weak one - the reverse of how this looked a week ago.

signals.headline: Rocket Lab's $663m of Space Force awards are dated 27 July and 4 August, not the past seven days
summary: The $266m record contract covers twelve guaranteed suborbital missile-defence launches from Alaska with options to eighteen, and is dated 27 July
The $397m award to build and launch Flatellites for the space-based airborne moving target programme is dated 4 August
The Flatellites launch on Neutron, which has never flown and whose slip into 2027 is the condition that would break the space case
signals.assessment: Trade coverage presented both as fresh across six outlets; the larger one depends on the exact catalyst that is at risk.

signals.headline: Saudi Arabia's $1.16bn battery award reconciles across its two separately reported halves
summary: Four storage service agreements signed 21 August worth SAR 4.35bn for 2,000MW over four hours on a build-own-operate basis
Saudi Energy with ACWA Power and Al Sharif took three 500MW sites for SAR 3.25bn - about $867m - and ENGIE with a local partner took the fourth for SAR 1.1bn; the two sum to SAR 4.35bn
A second tranche of about 12,000MWh, reported near $3.6bn, has entered bidding
signals.assessment: Two independently reported tranches that add up to the headline is the strongest corroboration available, and it is arithmetic rather than a second outlet.

signals.headline: Britain and Europe added grid-battery contracts in the same week as the Gulf award
summary: Arenko will deploy its platform at Orsted's 300MW Iceni project and NextEnergy acquired a 107MW UK portfolio
Waldevar won the engineering contract for a 220MWh Romanian project and Enel began a 100MW grid-forming system in Chile
New Jersey opened a 150MW behind-the-meter programme and China's storage market doubled for a second consecutive year
signals.assessment: The procurement is global and the listed pure-play exposure still is not, which is what keeps this off the main list.

signals.headline: Saudi Arabia signs $1.16bn of contracts for 8,000MWh of battery storage
signals.src: Saudi Power Procurement Company via Reuters / Zawya / AGBI, 21 Aug 2026
summary: Four storage service agreements worth SAR 4.35bn for 2,000MW over four hours, on a build-own-operate basis
Three 500MW sites go to a Saudi Energy, ACWA Power and Al Sharif consortium; the fourth to ENGIE with a local partner
A second tranche of about 12,000MWh, reported near $3.6bn, has entered bidding
signals.assessment: Storage is being procured as firm capacity under long-dated contracts rather than as an energy-arbitrage asset, which is the change that makes it financeable at this size.

signals.headline: A hundred items read in agtech and nothing met the bar
summary: The week is local agricultural coverage, an awards programme and market reports; the only named round is Mafix at $5.4m for silicate-rock fertiliser
The median 2026 round is about $12m and the year's two largest, Halter at $220m and Tropic at $105m, are both dated March
Corporate venture from Bayer, Syngenta, Corteva and Cargill remains active
signals.assessment: A drying private funding climate is a stronger negative than an absence of news, and it is what this now rests on.

signals.headline: Fierce Biotech frames the Merck and Moderna readout as setting up an approval push
summary: The phase 3 INTerpath-001 result of 19 August met recurrence-free and distant metastasis-free survival endpoints in resected melanoma
Moderna rose about 8% and BioNTech 4% across 20-21 August; Tempus AI added roughly $3bn on its Personalis stake
METiS and WestVac partnered on AI-designed personalised mRNA cancer vaccines on 21 August
signals.assessment: The next milestone is a filing accepted rather than a readout reported, and twenty-four collected items is the thinnest life-sciences week here.

signals.headline: Bitcoin leaps past $75,000 and MicroStrategy closes at $112.39
summary: BTC $75,401 on the 21 Aug snapshot, +8.86% and +19.64% on the week - which would be its biggest weekly gain since March 2024
MSTR closed $112.39 on 20 August, +7.81%, after BTC broke $71,000 intraday for the first time since May and forced a wave of short covering
The flag called exit at $91.39 on 14 July with a stated invalidation of BTC >$70k or MSTR >$110. The MSTR leg triggered on a settled close: +23.0% against the call
signals.assessment: Two independent sources put the 20 August close at $112.39, up 7.81% on the session, and a third records a 7.1-8.5% gain. Bitcoin's settled 20 August point is $69,266.19 and it went on to settle 21 August at $78,335.

signals.headline: CLARITY Act enactment odds halve even as the White House pushes it, to about 15.5% from about 30%
summary: Galaxy Research separately cut its odds of 2026 enactment from 50% to 30%
15 September is a FIRST PROCEDURAL VOTE at 2:15pm ET, not final passage; 60 votes are needed against 53 Republicans
The unresolved issue is ethics language preventing senior officials, including the President, from profiting from crypto
signals.assessment: Polymarket's 2026 enactment odds fell to about 15.5% from roughly 30% a week earlier and Galaxy Research cut its own estimate from 50% to 30%. The Senate has since pushed the bill to the autumn, with the procedural vote ripening 15 September.

signals.headline: Bitcoin tops $69,000 for the first time since June; ~$1.44bn of shorts liquidated
summary: BTC $69,381 on the 20 August fetch (+7.27%), after roughly $1.44bn of short positions were liquidated
Drivers cited are macro rather than crypto-native: the Treasury buyback expansion, a bond rally and a softer dollar
Trump publicly urged Congress to advance crypto market-structure legislation; an SEC crypto proposal is also cited
signals.assessment: Raises the crypto theme 2 to 3, and puts the MSTR exit flag's stated stated breaking condition (BTC above $70k) within 0.9%.

signals.headline: US agencies warned that AI-generated exploit scripts are being aimed at Siemens controllers in critical infrastructure
signals.src: CISA / NSA / FBI via Industrial Cyber and The Hacker News
summary: The advisory covers Siemens S7 programmable logic controllers in US industrial processes
Separately, US authorities warned on 20 August that attackers are using AI against vulnerable water utilities
MLflow, a machine-learning platform downloaded 30 million times a month, entered the exploited catalogue - the first AI development tool to appear on it
signals.assessment: The attack surface has moved into the physical plant and the AI toolchain in the same week, which is a change in kind rather than in volume.

signals.headline: US authorities say attackers are using AI to target vulnerable water utilities
summary: The warning follows six actively exploited flaws catalogued between 18 and 20 August, including the first AI-lifecycle tool
A VMware vCenter flaw was used by a suspected China-linked group to backdoor 361 victims across 47 countries
signals.assessment: The attack surface is widening in two directions at once - into the AI toolchain and into physical infrastructure - which is what keeps this a spending story rather than a licence-renewal one.

signals.headline: CISA adds an actively exploited PAN-OS flaw to KEV - Unit 42 says exploitation began 17 May
summary: CVE-2026-0257, CVSS 7.8 - lets an attacker bypass restrictions and establish VPN connections to vulnerable appliances via GlobalProtect
Exploited for weeks before it was known; KEV listing requires federal agencies to patch rapidly
Microsoft's August 2026 Patch Tuesday addressed 415 vulnerabilities, including one exploited zero-day, three disclosed zero-days and 62 critical
signals.assessment: Demand evidence for the category and a two-way risk for the named vendor, which reports on 1 September. CrowdStrike reports 26 August.

signals.headline: UK weapons and ammunition employment rose 51% as the wider defence industry added 26,000 roles
signals.src: UK Ministry of Defence via Defence Industry Europe / UK Defence Journal
summary: Ministry figures published in the week to 22 August
Rolls-Royce opened a regional defence headquarters in Canberra and Rheinmetall an autonomy centre in Britain earlier in the month
Germany is planning a EUR 12bn long-range missile programme and Switzerland added CHF 970m to air defence for 2026
signals.assessment: A British employment series is a slower and harder measure of rearmament than an order announcement, and it points the same way.

signals.headline: Rheinmetall trades about 42% below last October's high with the backlog above EUR 80bn
summary: Close near EUR 1,156 on 20 August inside a 52-week range of EUR 900.20 to EUR 2,008.00, and down about a third over twelve months
Q2 revenue EUR 3.289bn, up about 69%, with operating profit up 115%; first-half free cash flow was negative EUR 1.6bn
Bundeswehr documents flag maturity gaps: the Skyranger 30 has slipped from mid-2026 to mid-2027 and the Boxer is eleven months behind contract
signals.assessment: A record order book and a share price a third lower is the definition of an opportunity that is largely priced. The demand case is intact; what has been repriced is delivery and cash conversion.

signals.headline: Sixty items read in edge AI and no catalyst with a named listed beneficiary
summary: The window is vendor announcements, conference stands and market reports; the named hardware is still Snapdragon-generation from January and March
The nearest candidate is Advantech's industrial vision systems on Qualcomm's Dragonwing IQ9, announced 24 August, which is an integrator packaging an existing platform
Duos signed a $111m edge data-centre deal and Smack Technologies raised a $61m Series B for tactical edge AI
signals.assessment: Nothing met the bar on sixty observations rather than on two searches, which is a different quality of evidence for the same conclusion.

signals.headline: The US Treasury will detail its toughest Iran sanctions yet on Monday 24 August
summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on 20 August that Washington would set out what he called the toughest sanctions in history, aimed at Iran's trading partners
The campaign is described as shifting from military to economic pressure as the war nears its six-month mark
Tehran has criticised the package in advance as an assertion of extraterritorial sovereignty
signals.assessment: The energy premium has stopped transmitting into new markets, so it is now tested by whether it holds. Monday is the first of two dated tests.

signals.headline: The UAE suspends all trade and financial transactions with Iran after two ballistic missiles
summary: Two ballistic missiles were fired from Iran toward the UAE on 18-19 August, one landing in its territorial waters; the UAE defence ministry assessed both as targeting maritime traffic
The UAE had been a major trading partner for a sanctioned Iran; Tehran categorically denies launching them
Brent settled 20 August at $93.78, +2.36% on the day and +5.61% on the week
signals.assessment: The UAE suspended all trade, commercial exchange and financial transactions with Iran on 19 August after two ballistic missiles landed on its territory. The regional counterweight to the sanctions campaign narrows further.

signals.headline: Zinc hit a four-year peak and copper a record while smelting fees collapsed to zero
summary: Copper reached a record high while treatment charges fell to zero, leaving smelters dependent on gold, silver and sulphuric acid by-products
Aluminium rebounded on a supply deficit and on talk of a US-Canada tariff rollback; nearly sixty members of Congress have called for an aluminium pricing investigation
The IEA doubled its cobalt deficit forecast on Congolese export curbs and Zimbabwe's lithium concentrate ban takes effect in January
signals.assessment: Talk of rolling back the 50% metals tariffs is the first movement toward the condition that would break the reshoring case, and it is talk.

signals.headline: The KOSPI's break is reversed - up 5.89% to 6,853 on 20 August
summary: Reverses the 5.55% fall to 6,488.24 of 19 August almost exactly; Samsung up over 4% and SK hynix over 7%
Korea remains roughly 27% below the 9,385.59 record it set in June - the drawdown is not repaired, but the break is closed
Chip shipments reported at ~$26bn in the first twenty days of August, nearly triple the year-ago figure (one source, logged with a re-check)
signals.assessment: The index then rose 0.88% to 6,912.95 on 21 August, a second consecutive gain, and the arithmetic checks: 6,853 + 60.37 = 6,912.95. Korea remains about 26% below its June record of 9,385.59.

signals.headline: China leaves loan prime rates unchanged for a 15th consecutive month
